- **WHEP fails for a LAN viewer against the dockerized stack only when `VISION_WEBRTC_HOST` is left unset — this is expected, not a bug, and it's now the operator's choice, not a hard limit** (docs/MVP2-PLAN.md §L, and §V's V-e, which closed this gap after this Gotcha was first written). mediamtx in Docker advertises `127.0.0.1` ICE candidates by default (`MTX_WEBRTCADDITIONALHOSTS: "${VISION_WEBRTC_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"` in `docker-compose.yml`), so with `VISION_WEBRTC_HOST` unset, a browser on a *different* machine than the Docker host still always fails the WHEP exchange and silently lands on HLS via `Player`'s fallback (`shared/player/player-recovery.ts#reduceTransportRecovery`) — this is the entire reason that fallback exists and is treated as load-bearing, not an edge case. Setting `VISION_WEBRTC_HOST` in `.env` to the Docker host's own real LAN IP (see `vision-app/MODULE.md`'s "WHEP viewing" section for how an operator finds it and how to list more than one) makes WHEP work for LAN viewers pointed at that IP too, not just same-host ones. Don't "fix" a LAN demo showing `HLS` in the transport chip without first checking whether `VISION_WEBRTC_HOST` is actually set for that stack — an unset value is still expected same-host-only behavior, not a bug; once it *is* set, only a viewer entirely off that configured LAN/host (a different network, cellular data, a remote friend) should still show `HLS`. This app (`vision-web`) needed no change for V-e — the player's existing try-WHEP-then-HLS fallback already covers both the unset and the off-LAN cases identically; V-e is purely a compose/`.env` configuration lever.
- **`shared/player/player.ts`'s WHEP path gathers ICE non-trickle** (`waitForIceGatheringComplete`, bounded to `ICE_GATHERING_TIMEOUT_MS`=3s) rather than implementing WHEP's optional trickle-ICE PATCH exchange — simpler, and irrelevant to the LAN caveat above (a hung/incomplete gather just means a candidate-poor offer, not a different failure mode). If a future cycle needs faster/more-complete ICE negotiation, trickle is the documented gap, not a bug.
- **`shared/map/flight-plan-dialog.ts` is a modal (`position: fixed`, `z-index: 150`)**, not a page section — deliberately mounted only via `@if` in each host page's template (not always-in-DOM-but-hidden) so its own `afterNextRender` (and therefore Leaflet's `import('leaflet')`) only fires once the dialog is actually opened, matching every other map component's "chunk fetched on first use" convention. `150` sits above the toast host (`z-index: 100`) and the app header (`20`) on purpose — a toast fired while the dialog is open would otherwise render behind it; the dialog itself never toasts, so this is mostly theoretical, not exercised today.
- **`DiscoveredDevice.suggestedCategory` stays a bare `string`.** Even though `Category` is now mirrored (docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §2), discovery's suggestion is still typed as a plain slug, not `Category`/an enum — there is still no page that lists `GET /api/categories` to validate against, so don't tighten this without adding that consumer first.
- **Leaflet's own CSS is loaded at runtime, not imported as a component stylesheet.** `public/leaflet/leaflet.css` is a manual copy of `node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet.css` (kept in sync by hand when the `leaflet` version bumps — there is no build step that does this automatically); `angular.json`'s `assets` glob copies it to `dist/leaflet/leaflet.css` like any other static asset. `shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts#ensureLeafletStylesheet()` (shared by both `LiveMap` and `FleetMap` since docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §6) injects a `<link>` pointing at it the first time a map is created; idempotent, so either component can call it regardless of which one's map is created first. This is deliberate: importing the real file (14.8 kB raw) as a component `styleUrl` would trip the `anyComponentStyle` budget (10 kB error) and, if imported globally instead, would grow the initial bundle — a runtime-injected `<link>` to a plain static asset is invisible to both.
- **`::ng-deep` in `live-map.css` and `fleet-map.css`** targets DOM Leaflet creates itself (tiles, custom marker/popup/flag divIcons) — those elements never get Angular's `_ngcontent-*` attribute because Angular didn't render them, so emulated view encapsulation would otherwise silently no-op those rules. Still the standard, if deprecated, workaround for third-party-owned DOM inside an Angular component; scoped under `:host` to limit its reach. Each component still carries its **own** copy of the small rules that give Leaflet-owned elements their look (e.g. `.drone-arrow`'s geometry/color) — `shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts` shares the *JS* that builds/configures Leaflet objects, but per-component scoped CSS can't be shared the same way, so this one bit of duplication is intentional. `fleet-map.css`'s popup rules also lean on global classes (`.chip`, `.btn`) from `src/styles.css` for the parts that match existing chip/button styling — those aren't `::ng-deep`'d because a *global* stylesheet already reaches Leaflet-owned DOM without needing to. **The `vision-tiles`/`DARK_TILE_CLASS` CSS-invert dark tint is gone** (docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §9, CU-b item 6) — "dark" is now the real CARTO Dark Matter tile layer (`Night`, the default), not a filter over OSM; don't reintroduce the filter if OSM ever needs re-tinting for some other reason without checking whether a `Night`-style real layer is the better fix first.
- **`allowedCommonJsDependencies: ["leaflet"]`** in `angular.json` — Leaflet ships UMD only (no `module`/`exports` field), so without this the build emits (non-fatal) "not ESM, can cause optimization bailouts" warnings.
- **`InMemoryTelemetryRepository#findByUsage` (vision-app, not this module) returns the *first* `limit` samples of an ever-growing list, not the most recent.** At the sim's 1 Hz, a usage older than ~200 s will make `GET /api/usages/{id}/telemetry?limit=200` keep returning the same frozen earliest window forever, so `TelemetryStore.latest()`/`sampleAgeSeconds()` will appear to go stale permanently past that point in a long-running demo. This is a backend devsupport-adapter limitation (out of `vision-web/**`'s scope to fix), not a frontend bug — worth knowing before blaming the OSD's staleness indicator. `features/asset-detail/asset-detail-logic.ts#groupTelemetryByDevice`/`freshestSample` (docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §11) read from the exact same `usageTelemetry` response, so the asset detail page's per-device panels/"source: …" caption inherit this identical frozen-window ceiling — not a new bug, the same one wearing a new UI.
- **CDK virtual scroll (`features/devices/devices.ts`, docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §11) is this app's first actual use of `@angular/cdk`** beyond it sitting in `package.json` unused (it was pinned ahead of time for exactly this — see WEB-PLAN W6). `*cdkVirtualFor` is a classic structural directive (not the newer `@for` control-flow block — Angular has no virtualized `@for` equivalent), so it coexists in the same template as `@if`/`@for`/`@switch` elsewhere on the page without conflict; the one real constraint is that `<cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport>` needs a **fixed height** (`.asset-viewport`, `height: min(64vh, 26rem)`) and becomes its own self-scrolling region — a deliberate, necessary break from this page's otherwise full-document scroll, not an oversight.
- **`shared/map/live-map.ts` used to live at `features/live/live-map.ts`.** Moved in docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §11 (CD-b) when `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts` needed the identical single-asset map inset — see that file's own MODULE.md entry and `core/fleet/device-logic.ts`'s doc comment for the "no page imports another page's module" precedent this follows. If a search for `live-map.ts` under `features/` comes up empty, this is why — it's under `shared/map/`, not any one feature folder (and `pages/` no longer exists at all, per the folder-structure migration note above).
- **`@angular/cdk/scrolling` alone costs ~17 kB raw / ~4 kB transfer of *eager* bundle**, confirmed by isolating it (temporarily stripping the import and its one call site, rebuilding, restoring) — this is what pushes the initial bundle from 284.67 kB (before this cycle) to 301.91 kB, past the 300 kB *warning* threshold (not the 360 kB error one, which stays comfortably out of reach). None of it is `@angular/cdk/scrolling`'s own code appearing in an eager chunk *by name* (grep for `CdkVirtualScroll`/`ScrollDispatcher`/etc. in the initial chunks finds nothing — post-minification identifiers don't preserve those names), so this is very likely the module's own base dependencies (`Platform`, bidi/RTL support) that Angular's build resolves into a shared vendor chunk regardless of how few lazy chunks reference them. This is a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight: docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §11 item 4 explicitly asks for "CDK virtual scroll on the asset list", and this is the first time this app has used any `@angular/cdk` submodule beyond what shipped inert in `package.json` — the cost is real but the warning margin (1.91 kB over 300, vs. a 60 kB cushion to the 360 kB error) leaves comfortable room.
- **`PollScheduler`'s heartbeat is 1 s (`TICK_MS`, `core/poll-scheduler.ts`).** Every cadence registered via `schedule(periodMs, callback)` should be a multiple of 1,000 ms (every current caller's is: 1s/2s/5s) — a period that isn't lands on the next tick at or after its due time, not exactly on it, which is a few-hundred-ms slip once, not a growing drift (each task's own `nextDueAt` is recomputed from the tick that actually ran it, not from a fixed schedule).
- **`M` toggles the Live page's map inset** (docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §9, CU-b item 4) via a page-scoped `document` `keydown` listener in `LivePage`'s constructor — ignored while an `INPUT`/`TEXTAREA`/`SELECT` has focus or a modifier key is held, and removed on `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, so it can never fire from another route. Keep that ignore-list in sync if a future page adds more form-field-like custom elements. **`FlyPage` (docs/MVP3-PLAN.md §C-b) has its own, separate copy of this exact idiom**, extended to `M`/`B`/`F`/`Esc`/`?` — not shared with `LivePage`'s, since the two pages' shortcut sets and guard conditions (Fly's is picker-vs-cockpit-gated too) already diverge and a shared "keyboard shortcut registry" abstraction wasn't judged worth building for two five-line listeners.
- **The map-tile cache's `fetch()` reads depend on the tile host answering with a CORS header — verified against all four current providers, not assumed** (`shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts`'s tile-cache section above has the `curl -I` results). A bare `<img src>` (what every map used before this cache existed) never needed CORS at all; reading the response bytes into a `Blob` to store them does. If a future map layer is added pointing at a tile host that doesn't send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, that layer still renders correctly (`resolveTileSrc`'s `catch` falls back to a plain `<img src>`) — it just silently never gets cached. Don't add a fifth `MapLayerDef` without checking its own CORS headers first if caching that layer matters.
- **`FlyPage`'s cockpit CSS reaches into `<vision-player>`'s own DOM via `:host ::ng-deep .stage-video vision-player .frame`** (`fly.css`) to drop the player's normally-fixed 16:9 box so the video can genuinely fill the viewport — the first time this app's `::ng-deep` technique (previously only used for Leaflet-owned DOM, see the entry above) has been pointed at another Angular component's own template instead. Safe because the override only changes sizing (`height: 100%; aspect-ratio: unset`), never `object-fit` — the inner `<video>` keeps its own `contain` letterboxing regardless of the frame's shape, so no distortion. If `shared/player/player.ts`'s `.frame` class is ever renamed, this rule silently stops matching (the cockpit would quietly revert to a 16:9-boxed player, not throw) — grep for `.stage-video vision-player` if `player.ts`'s own CSS is ever restructured.
- **`navigator.sendBeacon` cannot send a WHEP `DELETE`** (docs/REALTIME-PLAN.md Phase R-b item 2) — `sendBeacon` can only ever issue an HTTP `POST`; mediamtx's session resource only accepts a real `DELETE` verb (`internal/servers/webrtc/http_server.go`'s router: `case http.MethodDelete: s.onWHIPDelete(...)`, no fallback for a POST-as-delete convention). This is why `shared/player/player.ts`'s `pagehide` handler uses `fetch(sessionUrl, {method: 'DELETE', keepalive: true})` instead — don't "simplify" this to `sendBeacon` without first confirming mediamtx (or whatever WHEP server is in front) grew a POST-based teardown convention; as of `v1.19.2` it hasn't.
- **The WHEP ICE-restart-via-PATCH flow (`shared/player/webrtc-ice-restart.ts`, docs/REALTIME-PLAN.md Phase R-b item 1) was derived directly from mediamtx's own Go source, not the WHIP/WHEP IETF drafts alone** — `internal/servers/webrtc/session.go`/`http_server.go` at tag `v1.19.2` were fetched (`curl` against `raw.githubusercontent.com`) and read in full before writing a single line of the client-side fragment logic; every function there cites the exact server-side counterpart it mirrors. mediamtx's **own bundled reference WHEP client** (`internal/servers/webrtc/reader.js`, served at `<path>/whep` in a browser) does **not** implement this flow at all — it only ever trickles candidates under the connection's *original* ICE ufrag and falls back to a full teardown+re-POST (a fixed 2s `RETRY_PAUSE`, no grace period) on any `connectionState` failure. If mediamtx's own source or bundled client is ever re-checked against a newer tag than `v1.19.2`, re-verify this flow still matches — there is no upstream reference implementation of ICE-restart-via-PATCH to diff against, only the server's own request-handling logic.
- **`await`ing a `setRemoteDescription`/`setLocalDescription` call is not a safe place to assume nothing else has happened yet — a live soak test caught `ontrack` racing ahead of the very next line 100% of the time (docs/REALTIME-PLAN.md Phase R-b follow-up).** `beginWhepAttach` used to call `scheduleWhepNoTrackTimeout()` only *after* `await pc.setRemoteDescription(...)` resolved, on the (reasonable-looking, wrong) assumption that "the timer starts, then either `ontrack` fires and clears it, or it doesn't and fires" — but on a fast/loopback connection, `pc.ontrack` fires as part of the browser *applying* the remote description itself, which can complete (and dispatch the event) before the `await`'s own JS continuation gets a turn to run. The result: a no-track timeout armed *after* the track had already arrived, with nothing left to ever clear it, firing unconditionally 6s later against a perfectly healthy stream — **every single attach**, confirmed at ~90 reproductions with near-zero jitter, tearing WHEP down and re-POSTing every ~7.15s (worse than the pre-plan baseline this entire plan exists to fix). **Fixed** with a per-attach `Player#whepTrackArrived` flag, checked by `player-recovery.ts#isWhepStillWaitingForTrack` at *both* the "should I arm this timer" call site and the timer's own fired callback — not by reordering alone (the call site *was* also moved earlier, but that only narrows the window; nothing stops the same event from firing even earlier still, so the flag check is what actually closes it). **The general lesson, worth remembering for any future WHEP/negotiation code in this file**: never assume an `await`ed WebRTC promise's continuation runs before a *related* event the browser might dispatch as a side effect of that same operation — always re-check actual observable state (a flag, `pc.getReceivers()`, `pc.connectionState`, etc.) immediately before acting on a timer/callback that was armed speculatively.
- `frontend-maven-plugin` provisions a **pinned** Node/npm into `target/node` per the `pom.xml` properties (`node.version`, `npm.version`) — doesn't use whatever Node is on `PATH`.
- `dist/` (Angular build output) is copied verbatim into `target/classes/META-INF/resources` by `maven-resources-plugin` in `prepare-package`; nothing here compiles Java (`No sources to compile` in `mvn` output is expected, not a failure).
- **`AssetDetailPage`'s telemetry-tracking effect re-entered `TelemetryStore.track()` 50–90×/sec — a self-sustaining loop, not paced by the 5s asset poll — confirmed live via CDP against the running `ng serve` (docs/REALTIME-PLAN.md §4 Phase R-c follow-up).** `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts`'s telemetry/detections constructor effects called `track()` unconditionally on every run (unlike `fly.ts`'s already-guarded twin — see the "Signals compare with `Object.is`" Gotcha above), so every ~5s `asset()` reference-churn tick re-entered it with the *same* `deviceId`/`assetId`. That alone would only have reproduced the slower R-a-class burst — the actual amplification was worse: `TelemetryStore.track()` → `startTracking()`'s synchronous prologue (`teardownTracking()`) reads the store's own private `currentAssetIdSignal` *while the caller's effect is still the active reactive consumer*, so that read gets attributed to the *caller's* effect, not the store's internal one. Once `startTracking()`'s async continuation later writes a real (non-`undefined`) value to that same signal, it re-notifies the caller's effect — with `asset()`/`assetTelemetryDevices()` unchanged (confirmed via a throwaway diagnostic instrumentation: ~130 consecutive re-runs in 3s, `assetRefChanged`/`devicesArrRefChanged` both `false` on all but the first) — which re-enters `track()`, repeating the read+write and closing a loop paced only by how fast the store's two lookups resolve (~30–45ms locally). `/live/:deviceId`/Wall are unaffected only because those callers never pass an `assetId` at all, so that same signal is written `undefined→undefined` every time — a no-op `Object.is` comparison that never re-notifies anything; this is incidental immunity, not a guard. **Reproduced live, not just reasoned about**: headless Chrome via CDP against a real, already-running `/api/live` SSE backend in this environment (`vision.live.enabled` is on here — the R-c Status entry's own "404-fallback" assumption is stale) captured 721 `[live] track/untrack telemetry:<assetId>` console lines *and 721 real PATCH `/api/live/{connectionId}/topics` requests* in 11.5s (62.6/sec) — **this was already a live PATCH storm against a real backend in this environment, not merely a future risk once one exists.** **Fixed, defense in depth at both layers**: (1) caller-side — `AssetDetailPage`'s telemetry/detections effects now guard with `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts#trackingIdChanged` exactly like `fly.ts`'s (`lastTelemetryDeviceId`/`lastDetectionsStreamId` fields), the primary fix, since it stops `track()` from ever being re-entered with an unchanged id at all; (2) ref-counting layer — `TelemetryStore`/`DetectionsStore.track()` themselves now no-op on an unchanged `(deviceId/streamId, assetId)` key (`lastTrackKey`, keyed via the new `core/live/live-fallback-logic.ts#trackSessionKey`), so an unguarded call site (`LivePage`/`WallTile` today; anything added later) can't reopen this class of loop even without its own guard. `trackingIdChanged` moved from `features/fly/fly-logic.ts` to `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts` (re-exported from `fly-logic.ts` for its own existing import site, tests moved with it) — the established "second consumer needs it, move it to core/" precedent (see `groupTelemetryByDevice`/`batterySeverity` above). New tests: `telemetry-store.spec.ts`/`detections-store.spec.ts` each gained an "N successive `track()` calls with the same id — even with no caller-side guard — subscribe live exactly once and never untrack" case (the exact churn class this bug was); `live-fallback-logic.spec.ts` gained `trackSessionKey` coverage. **Verified fixed live**: re-ran the identical CDP repro against `ng serve` after the fix — zero `[live] track/untrack telemetry:...` lines and zero PATCH requests over the same window for an unchanged asset. `ng serve` on `:4200` was left running throughout, untouched (same PID before/after, verified via `ss -ltnp`).
- **`shared/ui/events-rail.css`'s `.event-meta`/`.event-time` flex row let a long, unbreakable device/asset name (e.g. `X2Twitter.com_hzTcxvzE2-narxmk_720p`, a real simulated-source filename) overflow past its own box and visually overlap `.event-time`/`.event-affordance` at Wall's 300px sidebar (`wall.css`).** Root cause: neither the name nor its containing elements had `min-width: 0` (a flex item's default `min-width: auto` is its content's own minimum size — for an unbreakable token, that's its full rendered width) or any `overflow`/`text-overflow` handling, so the text simply rendered past its box rather than shrinking or wrapping. **Fixed**: the row is now two lines — an unshrinkable top line (state chip, label, time, action; all `flex: none` except `.event-label`, which truncates with ellipsis rather than overflowing if a long relative-time string squeezes it) and a full-width `.event-meta` line below for the source name + confidence, so the name gets the *entire* row's width to truncate against instead of whatever `.event-row-top` has left over (confirmed live: at Wall's 300px sidebar the name previously had ~5px available — invisible — vs. ~225px now, comfortably legible before needing to ellipsize). `.event-source` truncates with `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` and carries the full name in a `title` attribute; `.event-confidence` stays `flex: none` so the `%` is never the part that gives way. Verified via CDP screenshots at both Wall's 300px sidebar (name truncates, e.g. `X2Twitter.com_hzTcxvzE2-narxmk…`) and Command's full-width embed (name renders in full) — no overlap at either.
- **Pre-existing, out-of-scope: `shared/map/fleet-map.ts`'s own layer switcher (`.controls.layers`, `top:0.5rem;left:0.5rem`) overlaps Leaflet's own default zoom control (also `topleft` — `L.map(...)` is constructed with no `zoomControl: false` option, `fleet-map.ts`'s own `initMap()`), confirmed live via a docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-c verification screenshot of the new full-bleed Command map** (the "Standard" layer button's own left portion renders behind the zoom control's opaque `+`/`−` box). **Confirmed pre-existing, not a regression from this cycle**: `git diff` against `shared/map/**` for this task is empty — this component was read, not modified (out of this task's own file scope: "don't rework fleet-map/live-map themselves") — so this exact collision already existed on the old `/map` page and the old Command dashboard's own embedded map section, unchanged by anything here. Flagged for whoever next touches `shared/map/fleet-map.ts`: either add `zoomControl: false` and a custom-positioned zoom control that respects `.controls.layers`' own corner, or move one of the two controls to a different corner (`L.control.zoom({position: 'topright'})` collides with the Recenter control's own `top:0.5rem;right:0.5rem` instead — whichever corner is chosen needs auditing against *all three* corner occupants, not just two).
- **Doc-comment staleness flagged by an earlier cycle — fixed by the infra+cleanup batch, 2026-07-24.** `shared/map/live-dock.ts` (the file whose own doc comment carried the worst of this staleness — "each host page (`MapPage`, and now `CommandPage`, …) guarantees at most one is ever rendered") is now **deleted outright** (see the `/map` fleet overview section above), so that particular comment is simply gone rather than fixed in place. `shared/map/fleet-map.ts`'s own doc comment ("`MapPage` resolves a clicked marker's `watch` output…", "activated/released here — `MapPage` owns that lifecycle") and `core/map/map-store.ts`'s own doc comment (naming `MapPage` as a co-consumer) were rewritten to name `CommandPage` as the sole current host and, for the events lifecycle, `shared/ui/notification-bell.ts` as the actual owner. `core/events/events-store.ts`'s own doc comment — the most substantively stale of the four, since it described "O(visible) discipline" as this store's defining trait when `shared/ui/notification-bell.ts`'s permanent `activate()` had already superseded it — was rewritten to describe the current always-on-in-practice reality directly (see the Detection events section's own "Update, docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-c" paragraph above). Left here as a worked example of the failure mode, not because it recurs: a doc comment describing *why* a design choice was made ages fine; a doc comment asserting *who else does this today* silently rots the moment that "who" changes, with no compiler to catch it.

M5 (web) of the plan's M1→(M2‖M3)→M4→M5 wave sequence — the backend (M1–M4: domain `Mark`/`GeoProjection`, persistence, `MarkService`, `MarksController` + the `marks` live topic) had already landed uncommitted in the working tree when this wave started; this wave is `vision-web/**` only, coded against that frozen contract. Full writeup (store merge semantics, colour-by-kind hue derivation, bearing/distance math, the two independent map-layer implementations, both hosts' marks panels, the roles/authz story) lives in the new `### src/app/core/marks/**` section above and the two Fly/Command section bullets it's linked from — this entry covers only what a changelog scan needs.

**Files**: new — `core/marks/mark-logic.ts`+`.spec.ts`, `core/marks/marks-store.ts`+`.spec.ts`, `features/fly/marks-panel.ts`/`.html`/`.css`, `features/command/marks-panel.ts`/`.html`/`.css`. Edited — `core/api/models.ts` (Mark types + `LiveEnvelope`'s `marks` branch), `core/api/vision-api.ts` (5 endpoints), `core/live/live-store.ts` (`markEvents` signal + `case 'marks'`), `shared/ui/icon-registry.ts`+`icon.spec.ts` (`target`/`flag`), `shared/map/live-map/live-map.ts`+`.css`, `shared/map/fleet-map/fleet-map.ts`+`.css`, `features/fly/fly-facade.ts`/`fly.ts`/`fly.html`/`fly-logic.ts` (`'marks'` added to `ToolRailPanelId`), `features/command/command-facade.ts`/`command.ts`/`command.html` (`'marks'` added to `CommandOverlay`), `src/styles.css` (global `.leaflet-tooltip` dark override).

**UI-architecture layering** (docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE-PLAN.md, landed concurrently — re-surveyed at wave start per the plan's own concurrency caution, not assumed stale): both `FlyFacade`/`CommandFacade` gained a public `readonly marks = inject(MarksStore)` (mirrors `FlyFacade.geofence`'s existing full-store-exposure shape) so `fly.html`/`command.html` wire the shared map's `[marks]`/outputs straight to it — the ROUTED pages (`fly.ts`/`command.ts`) themselves never inject `MarksStore` and pass `architecture.spec.ts` unmodified. Both `<vision-marks-panel>` components are non-routed presentational children (that guard's own carve-out, and its own named exemplar list: `flight-command-panel`/`telemetry-osd`/`wall-tile`/`pilots-card`) and inject `MarksStore` directly, mirroring `zones-panel.ts` injecting `GeofenceStore` directly and `flight-command-panel.ts` injecting `VisionApi` directly. **The one place the layering forced a real divergence from the geofence precedent**: `MarksStore` itself carries UI-orchestration state (`selectedMarkId`, `pendingKind`/`draft`) that a store "shouldn't" own by the letter of docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE-PLAN.md's layering diagram — done deliberately because create-by-map-click must coordinate two sibling DOM subtrees (the shared map, wired in the host page's own template; the marks panel, a separate child) with no facade-mediated path between them that wouldn't require either duplicating the coordination in both `FlyFacade`/`CommandFacade` or reaching across component boundaries. Zones never hit this because `GeofenceZoneDialog` draws on its own private mini-map, entirely self-contained within `ZonesPanel`'s own subtree. Documented in `MarksStore`'s own class doc comment, not just here. One consequence of the map inset and the marks drawer being independent siblings: a captured map click produces a `draft()` regardless of whether the drawer is open at that moment — both `fly.ts` and `command.ts` gained one small `effect(() => { if (this.facade.marks.draft()) { <open the marks overlay> } })` in their own constructors (reading `facade.marks` — a property access, not a direct `inject(MarksStore)` — so `architecture.spec.ts`'s guard is unaffected) so a draft never silently lands out of sight.

**Degrade-honesty specifics**: a failed `refresh()`/mutation never fabricates a value — `loaded()` still flips true on a failed initial GET (empty list, not a stuck spinner), every mutation toasts `describeHttpError` and leaves local state untouched, and `moveTo`'s drag-to-correct forces a revert-render on failure (see `core/marks/**`'s own section for the mechanism) rather than leaving a dragged-but-unconfirmed pin sitting in the wrong place. The bearing/distance readout renders `—`, never a fabricated distance, whenever either the selected mark or a known drone position is absent — confirmed there is genuinely no "home"/launch position modeled anywhere in this app's telemetry or asset data (grep-verified across `Telemetry`/`TelemetrySampleResponse`/`AssetDetails` before writing `FlyFacade.dronePosition`'s own doc comment), so the plan's own Open Q3 default ("drone-only, note the gap") is what's implemented, not a placeholder for a home reading nothing currently supplies.

Green: `npm run test:ci` = 88 files / 1416 tests total (+56 new: 24 `manual-control-logic.spec.ts` +
14 `manual-control-client.spec.ts` + 11 `rc-monitor-logic.spec.ts` + 7 `rc-monitor.spec.ts`); `npx tsc
--noEmit` clean on both `tsconfig.app.json`/`tsconfig.spec.json`; `ng build --configuration
production` clean. **Bundle delta** (isolated via a `git worktree add
--detach` baseline at the pre-this-session commit, not just read off one build): initial bundle
**unchanged** (364.64 kB raw / 104.26 kB transfer — everything this wave adds is reachable only from
the `fly` lazy chunk, nothing eager/`providedIn:'root'`); **`fly` chunk 74.26 kB → 83.67 kB raw
(+9.41 kB), 17.06 kB → 19.17 kB transfer (+2.11 kB)** — `manual-control-client.ts`/`manual-control-logic.ts`
+ the expanded `rc-monitor.ts`/`.html`/`.css` + `rc-monitor-logic.ts`.

Built the R5 wave of docs/RC-CONTROL-PHASE1-PLAN.md — the web half of the SITL RC relay, coded
against the plan's frozen §4 WebSocket contract while R4 (the backend half, same contract) landed in
parallel in the same working tree. See the permanent `core/rc/**` reference above for the full
`ManualControlClient`/`rc-monitor.ts` writeup; this entry is the changelog.

- **`core/api/models.ts`** gained the §4 frame shapes (`ManualControlChannelBinding`,
  `ManualControlEngageMessage`/`ChannelsMessage`/`ReleaseMessage` client→server,
  `ManualControlEngagedMessage`/`DeniedMessage`/`AckMessage`/`ReleasedMessage`/`WatchdogMessage`
  server→client) — mirrored here 1:1 per this file's own "the wire contract" convention, exactly
  like `LiveConnected`/`LiveEnvelope` (raw `EventSource` frames) already established; these arrive
  over a raw `WebSocket`, never `HttpClient`.
- **`core/rc/manual-control-logic.ts`/`.spec.ts`** (new) — pure frame/latency/rate math, see the
  reference bullet above.
- **`core/rc/manual-control-client.ts`/`.spec.ts`** (new) — `ManualControlClient`, the WS relay
  service. The spec drives a hand-written `MockWebSocket` test double (this suite's first WS mock,
  mirrors `PollScheduler.spec.ts`'s "first use of fake timers" precedent) through every frame type,
  the send-loop cadence (`vi.useFakeTimers()`), and all five deadman triggers — including one that
  builds `ManualControlClient` inside its own **child `EnvironmentInjector`**
  (`createEnvironmentInjector`) rather than registering it on `TestBed`'s root testing module, so the
  "destroying the client" test can destroy exactly that child injector (simulating the RC panel
  unmounting) without tearing down `TestBed`'s own root injector out from under the harness's
  automatic per-test teardown — the first spec in this app to exercise `DestroyRef.onDestroy` this
  way; worth reusing this pattern if a future spec needs to test another provider's teardown path.
- **`features/fly/rc-monitor-logic.ts`/`.spec.ts`** (new) — `engageDisabledReason`/`latencyLabel`/
  `channelBindingLabel`, mirrors `flight-command-panel-logic.ts`'s own component-adjacent split.
- **`features/fly/rc-monitor.ts`** — split from one inline-template component into
  `rc-monitor.ts`/`.html`/`.css` (the Phase-0 file was small enough to stay inline; R5's Take-control
  section roughly doubled it, past this app's own informal threshold for when a component earns
  separate template/style files — matches `flight-command-panel`'s shape). Gained `assetId`/
  `assetDisplayName`/`canCommand` inputs and the `providers` array's second entry
  (`ManualControlClient`, alongside the pre-existing `RcInputService`). The Phase-0 monitor markup
  (axes bars, switch pills) is byte-for-byte unchanged; the new "Take control" `<div class="rc-engage">`
  is a **sibling** of the connected/not-connected branch, not nested inside it — deliberately, so a
  mid-session gamepad disconnect (which flips that branch back to "not connected") doesn't also hide
  an in-progress watchdog/released notice the operator still needs to see.
- **`features/fly/rc-monitor.spec.ts`** (new, component-level — this wave's own explicit ask, an
  exception to this app's usual "pure-logic-only" component-spec precedent) — overrides
  `RcMonitor`'s `providers` array (`TestBed.overrideComponent(..., { set: { providers: […] } })`,
  the first use of that API in this suite) with duck-typed `FakeRcInputService`/
  `FakeManualControlClient` doubles exposing writable signals, then asserts the gated button/reason,
  the engaged state's rateHz/latency chips + channel map + RELEASE control, the denied reason text,
  and the watchdog-vs-explicit-release distinction in `released`.
- **`features/fly/fly.html`** — `<vision-rc-monitor>`'s mount gained the three new input bindings
  (`[assetId]="a.assetId"`, `[assetDisplayName]="a.displayName"`, `[canCommand]="facade.canShowCommands()"`),
  same `a`/`facade` already in scope for `<vision-flight-command-panel>` right above it.

**Design/dataviz choices**: no new chart — the latency/rate readouts follow the Phase-0 monitor's own
existing idiom (`.chip`/`.chip.ok`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` baked into `.chip` itself),
not `<vision-stat>` (that component's own doc comment reserves it for headline KPIs, explicitly
*not* small fast-ticking OSD-style numerals like a live latency readout). No new icon — reused
`gamepad` (already the drawer's own header icon) rather than touching the frozen `IconName` set/spec.

**Design decision — a toggle "Take control"/"RELEASE", not a press-and-hold "Hold to fly" deadman**:
the plan named hold-to-fly as the safer option "if feasible". Judged **not feasible here**: flying
via the physical transmitter needs both hands on its sticks, so a pointer-held browser button would
either need a third hand or force the operator to let go of a stick to keep the relay alive — exactly
backwards from what a deadman should encourage. The toggle is safe *because* of the many independent
deadman triggers already covering the "operator stopped paying attention" case (panel close, tab
hidden, gamepad disconnect, socket drop, server watchdog) — RELEASE itself stays a big, always-visible,
text-labeled `.btn.danger.big` while engaged, per the plan's own fallback requirement for the toggle
option.

**Degrade/error handling**: a malformed/unrecognized server frame is defensively dropped
(`parseManualControlServerMessage` → `undefined`), never thrown — a single bad frame can't tear down
the relay session. A capabilities/asset-load failure upstream (`FlyFacade.canShowCommands()` already
degrading to `false` on any capability-fetch error) simply disables Take-control with its own inline
reason — never a dead button, never a fabricated "commandable" state.

**Role-gating**: none beyond `canCommand` — the plan's frozen §4 auth model is a same-origin session
cookie the WS handshake rides automatically (`ManualControlHandshakeInterceptor`, vision-api, R4),
identical to every other call in this app; there is no separate role check to encode client-side, the
server's own scope/commandability gate is authoritative (`OUT_OF_SCOPE`/`NOT_COMMANDABLE`/
`UNSUPPORTED` `denied` codes).

**Dev parity (`vision.auth.enabled=false`)**: unaffected — the WS handshake resolves the same
unbounded dev principal every REST call already does (R4's own doc comments confirm this explicitly),
so nothing in this wave needed a dev-parity branch.

**Mismatch found vs. the frozen §4 doc, reconciled against R4's actual landed code (not just the
doc)**: the plan's own written contract lists exactly four `denied.code` values
(`OUT_OF_SCOPE`/`NOT_COMMANDABLE`/`UNSUPPORTED`/`ALREADY_ENGAGED`); R4's actual
`ManualControlWebSocketHandler` also sends `denied` with three handler-defensive codes
(`MALFORMED`/`UNKNOWN_TYPE`/`BAD_REQUEST`) for a frame it couldn't parse/route at all — its own
javadoc calls this out explicitly ("deliberately a plain string, not a closed enum on the wire").
This client's first cut validated `denied.code` against the closed four-value set, which would have
silently **dropped** those three frames (never surfacing `reason` at all) — found by reading R4's
actual landed DTOs/handler before finalizing this report, not just the plan doc, and fixed:
`ManualControlDeniedCode` widened to `string` (`models.ts`), `manual-control-logic.ts#isDenied` now
only checks that `code`/`reason` are both present strings. Every other frame shape/field name
(`ManualControlEngagedFrame`/`AckFrame`/`ReleasedFrame`/`WatchdogFrame`/`ChannelsRequest`, the
`/ws/manual-control` path, same-origin session-cookie auth) matched this client's own first-cut
implementation exactly — no other reconciliation needed. One documented rough edge on R4's side worth
knowing: `engaged.rateHz` is a fixed constant on the backend (`ManualControlEngagedFrame.DEFAULT_RATE_HZ`
= 33), not read live from the adapter's own `VISION_RC_OVERRIDE_HZ` env knob — this client already
throttles its own send loop to whatever `rateHz` the `engaged` frame actually says (`sendIntervalMs`),
so it is correct either way, just worth knowing the number won't move if that env knob is ever tuned
without also touching vision-api's own constant.

**Incomplete / left for the SITL verification step (this plan's own explicit "user-run, not CI"
section)**: no live SITL run happened in this task (no SITL instance, no RC transmitter in this
environment) — everything above is verified against R4's actual landed backend code (reconciling the
wire shapes) plus this app's own mocked-WebSocket test suite, not a live end-to-end session. The
plan's own §5 default channel map (ch1-4 axes Roll/Pitch/Throttle/Yaw, ch5-8 buttons Aux 1-4) is
rendered verbatim from whatever `channelMap` the `engaged` frame carries (this client invents nothing
client-side), so it will display correctly against R4 as landed, but the actual latency/watchdog
numbers, the "does the copter track the sticks" question, and the audit-trail verification are all
still the human's own SITL step per the plan.

## Status — design-token consolidation + repeatable-element components (docs/STYLE-TOKENS-PLAN.md) — 2026-07-30

Green: `npx ng build --configuration production` succeeds (no budget warnings after bumping `anyComponentStyle` maximumWarning 6→8 kB — tokenization trades short hex for longer `var(--color-*)` refs, so the per-file text budget moved with it; the 10 kB error ceiling is unchanged); **`npm run test:ci` = 76 files / 1274 tests pass**; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

Two threads, one pass:
1. **CSS design tokens (all of `src/styles.css` + every one of the 33 component `.css` + 21 inline-`styles` `.ts`).** Rebuilt `styles.css` into the two-tier color system (primitive ramp → semantic aliases — see the permanent "Design-token system" reference above), converted the spacing scale to a **strict rem 8px grid named by px** and migrated all ~87 old-`--space-N` consumers onto it, then swept every component to replace raw hex/`rgb()` with semantic tokens and every off-grid `px`/`rem` gap/padding with `--space-*`. Killed real palette drift (a rogue 2nd blue `#3b82f6` + a whole slate ramp living as `var(--x, #hex)` fallbacks in `fleet-map.css`; off-spec map bg `#0b0f14`→`--bg`) and a live bug (the Leaflet popup was styled with literal `gray`/`white`/`blue`). Fonts were already compliant (2 families, every `font-family` already `var(--font)`/`var(--mono)`). Remaining hex is only in JS paint constants (Leaflet `L.polyline({color})`, canvas `ctx.*Style`, `KEEP_OUT_COLOR`/`modelHue`) — those can't read CSS vars and legitimately stay literal. Audit-clean: zero raw hex in any component `.css`, zero `px` in any gap/padding, zero dead alias/space tokens.
2. **Four repeatable elements → shared components** (user rule: "if the element is repeatable, make it a component"): `<vision-notice>` (13 banners), `<vision-empty>` (empty states), `<vision-kebab-menu>` (kebab overflow, 30 sites), `<vision-stat>` (KPI tiles) — all in `shared/ui/`, standalone + OnPush + `input()` signals, unit-tested (11 cases across 4 spec files), documented in the shared/ui reference above. The `.chip` utility was deliberately **kept a CSS class** (92 sites, atomic — matches this repo's own convention, cf. the specialized `identity-chip`/`weather-chip` components). `vision-stat` follows the `dataviz` stat-tile contract (proportional semibold, not the telemetry mono register). Call sites migrated across assets/devices/asset-detail, onboarding/activity/org-settings, command/live/wall/login; overlay-positioned/borderless/single-use cases (e.g. the shell's one `.offline-banner`, command's `.stage-empty` map overlay) intentionally left bespoke.

Delegated in disjoint file-scope waves (this repo's own model): a foundation pass (this session, `styles.css` + the frozen contract doc), CSS token waves + element-migration waves fanned out to `web-ui` subagents, and a final cleanup (alias removal, audit, this doc). Full contract, hex→token crosswalk, and snap table: docs/STYLE-TOKENS-PLAN.md.

## Status — layered UI state: facades + UiStore across all features (docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE-PLAN.md) — 2026-07-31

Green: `npm run test:ci` = 78 files / 1293 tests; prod build clean; the routed-page guard grep clean
(no page component injects `VisionApi`/a `*Store` directly — only its facade).

Formalized the zoneless-signals app into a `Component → Facade → Store → Service` layering (NgRx
rejected — would fight the signals grain and rewrite ~11 working stores). Delivered as a foundation
(`UiStore` + exemplar) then a whole-app sweep in disjoint waves: **13 feature facades** created
(`fly`/`command`/`asset-detail`/`assets`/`devices`/`live`/`wall`/`replay`/`onboarding`/`org-settings`/
`activity`/`settings`/`login`); each routed page now injects only its facade. The consistency win —
mutually-exclusive overlays that were independent booleans (able to drift open) are now single
`UiStore` groups: `flight-command-panel`'s 3 confirms, `fly`'s stop-confirm, `command`'s zones, and
**`asset-detail`'s 4 editors** (`editingAsset`/`editingRegistrationNumber`/`attributesEditorOpen`/
`assignOpen`). Pure re-wiring — every HTTP call, toast, silent-degrade path, poll cadence, gate, and
persisted `localStorage` key is unchanged; verified by the full suite staying at 1293 green and a
manual review (asset-photo URL, restore-target state, panel-close timing all confirmed identical).

Not yet done (follow-up, per the plan's W5): the `core/ui/architecture.spec.ts` guard that fails CI on
a future violation; retiring the `PanelState` name where a few hosts still use it (API-compatible, so
harmless meanwhile). Delegated across parallel `web-ui` agents; two hit a transient `git stash`
collision in the shared tree and self-restored — tree integrity re-verified green after.

**Poll scheduler consolidation (item 3) — what merged and why:**
- **Merged into `PollScheduler` (`core/poll-scheduler.ts`, new):** `FleetStore`'s 5s device/stream poll; `TelemetryStore`'s 2s telemetry poll *and* its 1s age-readout clock; `FleetMapStore`'s 5s asset poll, its 1s age-readout clock, *and* every per-streaming-asset 2s telemetry tracker (a dynamic, N-instance case — each tracker registers/unregisters its own `schedule()` call as assets start/stop streaming); `DetectionsStore`'s 2s detections poll and its 1s CV-status clock. That is up to `1 + (1+1) + (1+1+N) + (1+1)` independent `setInterval`s on a busy `/map` tab, collapsed to **one** shared `setInterval` (`PollScheduler`'s own `TICK_MS = 1_000` heartbeat) — every consumer just registers `(periodMs, callback)` and gets called back on its own cadence. `DetectionsStore` wasn't named in the plan's literal item-3 list (`FleetStore`/`TelemetryStore`/`FleetMapStore`) but duplicates the exact same poll+clock idiom `TelemetryStore` already had (it was built to mirror it, per its own MODULE.md history) — merging it too was the obviously-intended reading of "extract the poll-while-visible idiom … into a single shared helper", not a scope add.
- **Minor behavior harmonization, called out explicitly:** the four 1s "age readout" clocks (`TelemetryStore`, `FleetMapStore`, `DetectionsStore` ×1 each) previously ran unconditionally, even while the tab was hidden; routing them through `PollScheduler` means they now pause with everything else while hidden. Harmless — nothing renders a "seconds ago" label while the tab is hidden anyway — and it's the more consistent behavior, not a regression.
- **Deliberately left alone, with reasons:** `ToastService`'s per-toast auto-dismiss `setTimeout` (one-shot, not recurring — nothing to "poll"); `shared/player/player.ts`'s `latencyTimer` (1s, samples HLS latency) and `retryTimer` (one-shot backoff for a missing first segment) — a *playback* measurement/retry concern tied to the video element's own lifecycle, not a "re-fetch from the backend while the tab is visible" poll, and it deliberately does **not** pause while hidden (a backgrounded tab's video should keep buffering); `features/live/live-map.ts`'s `setTimeout` after the expand/collapse CSS transition (one-shot, not recurring); `features/devices/devices.ts`'s `setTimeout` that clears the "highlighted" outline after using a discovery candidate (one-shot UI timing, not a poll); `core/idle-preload.ts`/`core/leaflet-warmup.ts`'s idle callbacks (browser idle scheduling, a different primitive from a recurring visible-tab poll, and each only ever fires once).
- **8 new spec cases** (`core/poll-scheduler.spec.ts`: 2 for the re-exported `shouldPoll` + 6 for `PollScheduler` itself, using `vi.useFakeTimers()` — the first use of fake timers in this suite; every other spec file relies on real short `setTimeout(…, 0)` flushes instead, but a scheduler literally about timing needs to control time to test cadence/pause/unsubscribe behavior without a multi-second real-time test): registration/cadence, multiple consumers on different cadences off one timer, pause-while-hidden without dropping the eventual call, unsubscribe stops calls, one consumer unsubscribing doesn't affect a sibling.

Also folded in docs/MVP2-PLAN.md **§U-info** (mid-task scope addendum — the plumbing-first "Source" card became `shared/player/stream-info-panel.ts`) since it touched the exact same Live-rail/asset-detail info surfaces this cycle was already rebuilding.

**New/moved files**: `core/fleet/warehouse-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`, generic lifecycle logic lifted from `features/devices/devices-page-logic.ts`), `core/stream-info-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`), `shared/player/player-recovery.ts` (+`.spec.ts`), `shared/player/detection-overlay-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`), `shared/player/stream-info-panel.ts`, `shared/map/live-map.ts`/`.html`/`.css` (moved from `features/live/`), `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts`/`.html`/`.css`, `features/asset-detail/asset-detail-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`). **Rewritten**: `shared/player/player.ts` (self-recovery + overlay canvas). **Reshaped**: `features/devices/devices.ts`/`.html`/`.css` (asset-first list + Advanced collapse), `features/devices/devices-page-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`, kept page-specific view models, added `AssetListRow`), `features/live/live.ts`/`.html`/`.css` (boxes toggle, `StreamInfoPanel`), `features/wall/wall-tile.ts` (`DetectionsStore` + boxes-cycle button), `features/map/map.ts`/`.html` (rail lists all assets + Open), `app.routes.ts` (`/assets/:id`), `core/api/models.ts` (`TelemetrySample.deviceId`).

**Player recovery, concretely**: `reduceRecovery(state, event)` is a pure reducer over `PlayerPhase = 'idle'|'connecting'|'waiting'|'playing'|'reconnecting'|'error'`. Before ever playing, a missing playlist (`playlistNotReady`) stays `waiting`, retried every 1.5s indefinitely (no cap — the old `FIRST_SEGMENT_RETRY_LIMIT=40` gave-up-after-40-tries behavior is gone, replaced by "poll until ready" per the plan's literal wording). Once attached, a stall watchdog (`isStalled`: no `FRAG_BUFFERED`/native `progress` event for 8s) or a genuine fatal error moves to `reconnecting`, which schedules a reattach after `reconnectDelayMs(attempt)` — capped exponential, 1s→2s→4s→…→30s, held at 30s indefinitely. `error` is now reached only for "this browser can play neither native HLS nor hls.js" — never for a transient network/backend hiccup, which is the whole point: the player never gives up on its own while `src` stays set, verified conceptually against "must survive a backend restart" (an outage of any length is just a longer run of 30s-spaced retries, not a terminal state).

**Detection overlay sync, concretely**: `selectDetectionResult(results, nowMs, latencySeconds, slackBatches=1)` estimates the on-screen frame's capture instant as `nowMs - latencySeconds*1000` (`latencySeconds` is `shared/player/player.ts`'s own measured `behindLive`, piped in as an input — never re-measured), then picks the newest of the newest-first `results` whose `capturedAt` doesn't run ahead of that instant, with one observed inter-batch interval of slack for scheduling jitter; falls back to the oldest result if every one looks "future" (the brief window right after attach before latency has settled). Boxes are drawn on a `<canvas>` sized to the video element's own box, mapped through `object-fit: contain`'s letterbox rect (`Player#letterboxRect`) so they land pixel-correct regardless of aspect ratio; hover hit-tests the last-drawn rects for a label+confidence tooltip.

**Multi-telemetry, concretely**: `TelemetrySampleResponse.deviceId` (CD-a, already server-side) means one usage's `GET /api/usages/{id}/telemetry` response can legitimately mix samples from more than one TELEMETRY-capable device. `groupTelemetryByDevice` regroups them by source for the asset detail page's per-device panels; the map, by contrast, deliberately keeps using `TelemetryStore.latest()`/`trail()` (the whole mixed stream, unfiltered) for its marker/trail — since the backend returns samples chronologically regardless of source, the *last* sample in that flat list already **is** the freshest across every source, which is exactly what item 3 asks the marker to show, with zero new store code needed. `freshestSample` (a separate, explicit "max by timestamp across per-device groups" computation, `O(devices)`) backs only the page's "source: <device name>" caption — a transparency nicety, not the map's actual position math.

- A handful of small unnamed shared chunks (34.83/7.42, 13.18/4.42, 10.95/3.79 kB and several sub-3kB ones) now carry code common to two or more of `wall`/`live`/`asset-detail`/`map` — most plausibly `shared/map/live-map.ts` (shared by `live` and `asset-detail`) and `Player`/`player-recovery.ts`/`detection-overlay-logic.ts` (shared by `wall`/`live`/`asset-detail`/the map dock) — esbuild's automatic chunk-splitting extracts code reachable from more than one lazy entry point into its own chunk rather than duplicating it, exactly the intended behavior; not independently named per route by the build, so attribution here is by elimination rather than exact.

**Deviations from the task's literal wording, with reasons**:
- **Item 6's "burned"/"off" boxes modes render identically** (both simply suppress the client-side canvas) — disabling the *server's* burn-in itself has no API today and is explicitly out of this cycle's scope ("no server change"), so there is no way to make the delivered video pixels show zero boxes; the two states differ only in what they claim about intent (trust the baked-in boxes vs. want no detection UI/hover at all), not in what's on screen. Documented, not silently swept under a single state.
- **Per-tile toggle on the Wall is a single cycling icon button** (`▢`/`▢·`/`▢×`), not a three-button group like Live/asset-detail's — a compact tile has no room for a labeled `Overlay/Burned/Off` button row; the cycling button still reaches all three states, just via repeated clicks with a `title` tooltip naming the current one.
- **The Devices page's asset list gets no new automatic poll.** Item 4 asks for `O(visible)` polling; this cycle interpreted that as "don't make the existing `O(total assets)` fetch (one `getAsset()` per asset, needed for `deviceCount`/`watchDeviceId`) recur automatically on a timer" rather than as "add a poll, but keep its per-tick cost bounded" — an unconditional 5s poll of an O(total) fetch would be a worse scalability posture for "thousands of assets" than today's load-once/mutate/manual-Refresh cadence, given the backend's in-memory repositories (not this cycle's job — P-a/P-b, MVP2-PLAN) are the actual ceiling. The list still refreshes on every mutation and the existing Refresh button, unchanged from before this cycle.
- **"Battery when live" is omitted from the asset-first list's row decoration** (item 1 lists it as a nice-to-have alongside streaming status/device count). Showing it would need a `FleetMapStore`-style concurrency-capped per-streaming-asset telemetry poller at *list* scope — a meaningful new poller class for a decorative list column, when the same information is one click away (Watch, or the asset detail page's own per-device telemetry panels, which is the page whose entire job is telemetry). Streaming status and device count — the two facts genuinely useful for triage from the list itself — are both present.
- **docs/MVP2-PLAN.md §U-info's "dock panels" was interpreted narrowly**: `LiveDock` (the map's docked preview) did not gain the full `<vision-stream-info>` panel — that would need its own `DetectionsStore` instance for a panel that's explicitly a compact, bandwidth-conscious preview (`MapPage` already caps docked previews at one at a time). It keeps its existing compact OSD-style summary; the full user-meaning-first info panel is the Live rail's and the asset detail page's job, both of which this cycle did rework.
- **Resolution/FPS, called out by §U-info as a "video fact" to show**, are not shown anywhere — verified against every current DTO (`ActiveStreamResponse`, `DetectionResultResponse`, `BoundingBoxResponse`) that no endpoint exposes frame dimensions or a video FPS figure; per §U-info's own "implements what current APIs already serve" scoping, this is a documented gap for a future cycle that adds the field server-side, not a guess.
- **§U-info's "usage link"** (alongside the live-ticking duration) is not a clickable link anywhere yet — there is no usage-detail/replay page to point it at (that's R-b, MVP2-PLAN, a later cycle); the duration itself is shown, the link is deferred until somewhere exists for it to go.

## U3 — flight-plan map editor + WHEP-first playback (docs/CYCLES-PLAN.md §7 CT-b; docs/MVP2-PLAN.md §L/§U3)

Two independent features sharing one cycle: (A) a click-to-drop-waypoints map editor for the Simulate wizard's flight plans, replacing raw home-point fields (CT-b); (B) `shared/player/player.ts` tries WebRTC(WHEP) first when a stream's `whepUrl` is present, falling back to HLS automatically on any failure before a track arrives — integrated into the existing `player-recovery.ts` state machine, not built beside it.

**New files**: `shared/map/flight-plan-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`), `shared/map/flight-plan-dialog.ts`/`.html`/`.css`. **Reshaped**: `shared/player/player.ts` (WHEP attach path + transport-aware chip), `shared/player/player-recovery.ts` (+`.spec.ts` — `Transport`/`TransportRecoveryState`/`initialTransportState`/`reduceTransportRecovery`, additive only), `shared/player/stream-info-panel.ts` (new `transport` input), `core/stream-info-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts` — `transportLabel`), `core/api/models.ts` (`whepUrl?` on `ActiveStream`/`StartStreamResult`/`SimulationResponse`; `RouteMode`/`WaypointRequest`/`TelemetryPlanRequest`; `StartSimulationRequest.telemetry?`), `features/devices/simulate-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts` cases — `telemetry?` on `FileSimulateForm`) and `core/fleet/simulation-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts` cases — `telemetry?` on `TestDroneForm`), `features/devices/devices.ts`/`.html`/`.css` (Flight plan block + home-point fallback disclosure), `features/map/map.ts`/`.html` ("Draw a flight plan…" button), `features/wall/wall-tile.ts`, `features/map/live-dock.html`, `features/live/live.ts`/`.html`, `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts`/`.html` (all four thread `whepUrl` into `<vision-player>`; `live`/`asset-detail` also thread `transportChanged` into `<vision-stream-info>`).

**Flight-plan editor, concretely**: `FlightPlanDialog` is a modal (not embedded inline), reused verbatim from two unrelated pages exactly like `LiveMap`/`core/fleet/device-logic.ts` before it. Opening it seeds `seedTriangle(home)` — offsets derived once from `scripts/demo.sh`'s own demo triangle's shape relative to its centroid, reapplied near whichever home point the caller has (or San Francisco, as a generic fallback) — so hitting Save immediately produces a flyable 3-waypoint loop. Click the map to append a waypoint (numbered marker + dashed polyline, via the shared `shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts`); drag a marker (only `dragend` commits, so mid-drag doesn't fight the gesture by rebuilding markers on every pixel); per-waypoint altitude + Remove live in the list below the map; a collapsed manual `lat,lon[,altM]`-per-line text fallback covers "I'd rather type/paste than click" (CT-b's own spec text). Speed defaults to `12` m/s (the adapter's own default); route mode is the actual three-value `RouteMode` contract — **loop/bounce/once** — not the task brief's "loop/once" paraphrase (see Deviations). `buildTelemetryRequest` serializes the draft to the wire shape only at Save; `Devices`/`Map` thread it into `StartSimulationRequest.telemetry` via the existing `buildSimulationRequest`/`buildTestDroneRequest` builders' new optional `telemetry` form field — no new HTTP call, the existing `/api/simulations` POST just carries more.

**Transport state machine, concretely**: `player-recovery.ts`'s pre-existing `RecoveryState`/`reduceRecovery` (phase/attempt bookkeeping, capped backoff) are **completely unchanged** — every one of the 18 pre-U3 specs still passes verbatim. `reduceTransportRecovery(state: TransportRecoveryState, event)` wraps them with exactly one added rule: a `webrtc` transport failing (`fatalError`/`stalled`/`unsupported`) while its nested `recovery.phase` is `connecting`/`waiting` (i.e. it has never reached `playing`) falls over to `hls` permanently for the attach lifetime, restarting `hls`'s own recovery from a clean `connecting`; the same failure while `recovery.phase` is `playing`/`reconnecting` (i.e. it *has* played before) instead retries `webrtc` itself via `reduceRecovery`'s own capped backoff — "reconnect cycles per transport". This mirrors `reduceRecovery`'s own `playlistNotReady` precedent (`connecting`/`waiting` = "never played, be gentle" vs. everything else = "played before, this is a real reconnect") applied one level up, at the transport-choice layer instead of the phase layer. `shared/player/player.ts` drives this with a parallel WHEP attach path (`beginWhepAttach`/`handleWhepFailure`/`teardownWhep`) alongside the pre-existing HLS one (`beginAttach`, untouched in its own logic, only its recovery calls now go through `reduceTransportRecovery` instead of `reduceRecovery` directly): `RTCPeerConnection`, one recvonly video transceiver, non-trickle ICE (bounded 3s gather), POST the offer's SDP to `whepUrl` (`Content-Type: application/sdp`), apply the answer, wait for `ontrack` (bounded 6s — "no track within a timeout"). `behindLive` is pinned to `0` the instant a track arrives (a real number the detection-overlay matcher needs, not `null`) though the visible badge reads `'live · WebRTC'` rather than a falsely-precise `'0.0s behind'`. A WHEP-specific watchdog (`startWhepWatchdog`, same `isStalled`/`STALL_WATCHDOG_MS`=8s check as HLS's own) covers a later silent stall. `transportChanged = output<Transport>()` lets a host echo the live transport (`StreamInfoPanel`'s new "Transport" fact, `core/stream-info-logic.ts#transportLabel`, no longer hardcoded `"HLS"`).

**Test count: 247 → 288** (41 new — verified: 247 + 41 = 288, matches exactly):
- `shared/map/flight-plan-logic.spec.ts` — 22 cases (`seedTriangle`'s determinism/fallback, add/move/updateAltitude/remove waypoint ops, manual-text parse/format round-trip including lenient skip-bad-lines behavior, `canSavePlan`'s ≥2 minimum, `buildTelemetryRequest`'s omit-when-null/undefined-below-minimum/all-three-`routeMode`-values serialization).
- `shared/player/player-recovery.spec.ts` — 13 new cases on top of the 18 pre-existing, unmodified ones (`initialTransportState`'s webrtc/hls starting choice; `reduceTransportRecovery`'s fallback-before-playing for `fatalError`/`stalled`/`unsupported`, retry-on-transport-after-playing, no-late-fallback-while-already-reconnecting, hls-unchanged-behavior, terminal `error` reached correctly when hls itself is unsupported, and one full WHEP-attempt→fallback→HLS-plays→HLS-reconnects integration case).
- `features/devices/simulate-logic.spec.ts`/`core/fleet/simulation-logic.spec.ts` — 4 new cases (`buildSimulationRequest`/`buildTestDroneRequest` each: omits `telemetry` when absent, includes it verbatim — and, for the file-modes builder, confirms `latitude`/`longitude` still ride alongside a route since the backend ignores them in that case, not this function's job to suppress).
- `core/stream-info-logic.spec.ts` — 2 new cases (`transportLabel` for both transport values).
- No page-component-level specs for `devices.ts`/`map.ts`/`shared/map/flight-plan-dialog.ts`/`shared/player/player.ts`'s WHEP path — consistent with this app's existing precedent (every prior UI cycle's own Status entry makes the same call); exercised by the full production build (twice, from clean) and manual verification against this doc. `RTCPeerConnection`/`fetch`/Leaflet inside a modal dialog would need a much heavier component-test harness (fake media streams, fake ICE) than this app has ever invested in for `Player`'s existing hls.js path either.

**Bundle sizes** (`ng build --configuration production`, before → after; before = U2's own recorded "after" numbers above, i.e. the working state this cycle started from):
- **Initial total: 301.91 kB raw / 83.94 kB transfer → 301.91 kB raw / 83.94 kB transfer — unchanged, to the byte.** Every new module this cycle (`shared/map/flight-plan-logic.ts`, `shared/map/flight-plan-dialog.ts`, the `player-recovery.ts`/`player.ts` WHEP additions, `core/stream-info-logic.ts#transportLabel`) is reachable only from a lazy route chunk or a component those chunks import — none are `providedIn: 'root'` or otherwise eager. `models.ts`'s new fields/types cost nothing at runtime (types erase; the new optional wire fields are just more properties on interfaces `FleetStore`/`VisionApi` already ship).

- **`live`: 17.37 kB / 4.84 kB → 17.63 kB / 4.91 kB** (+0.26 kB / +0.07 kB — the `whepUrl`/`transportChanged` bindings + `transport` signal).
- **`asset-detail`: 24.53 kB / 6.47 kB → 24.80 kB / 6.52 kB** (+0.27 kB / +0.05 kB — same shape as `live`'s delta).
- **`wall`: 7.00 kB / 2.55 kB → 7.04 kB / 2.56 kB** (+0.04 kB — one new `[whepUrl]` binding, no new signal).

**Deviations from the task's literal wording, with reasons**:
- **Route mode is loop/bounce/once, not the task brief's "loop/once".** The brief's own parenthetical said "match the actual TelemetryPlan contract", and the actual contract (`vision-application.RouteMode`, CT-a) has three values; implementing only two would have been a narrower, incorrect mirror of a contract this cycle was explicitly told to match.

The task text said the empty-state action "can open the same dialog" (permissive, not "must replace") — replacing the existing one-click path would have regressed CU-b item 7's own explicit "one click, no hardware" requirement for the common case (most test-drone placements don't need a custom route); the dialog is additive for the case that does.

## R-b — flight replay cockpit (docs/MVP2-PLAN.md §R)

The asset detail page's usage history gains a **Replay** action on every finished usage: a new `/assets/:assetId/replay/:usageId` cockpit — map trail drawn up to a scrub position, a heading-rotated marker there, a play/pause/1×/4×/16× scrub bar with a detection-density strip, and telemetry/detections panels reading their values *at* the scrub time. Built against R-a/R-a2's already-shipped `GET /api/usages/{usageId}/timeline` (verified against `vision-api/MODULE.md`'s own §Replay entry and the controller/DTO source directly, not assumed).

**New files**: `features/replay/replay-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`), `features/replay/replay-map.ts`/`.html`/`.css`, `features/replay/replay.ts`/`.html`/`.css`. **Reshaped**: `app.routes.ts` (new route), `core/api/models.ts` (`UsageTimeline`), `core/api/vision-api.ts` (`usageTimeline`, +2 `vision-api.spec.ts` cases), `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts` (+`groupTelemetryByDevice`/`telemetryDevices`, moved from `features/asset-detail/asset-detail-logic.ts` — see below), `features/asset-detail/asset-detail-logic.ts` (now re-exports those two), `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.html` (usage history's new Replay/Watch-live column).

**A second page needing `groupTelemetryByDevice`/`telemetryDevices` triggered the same "lift to `core/`" move this codebase has made three times before** (`core/fleet/device-logic.ts#findVideoDevice`, `core/fleet/warehouse-logic.ts`'s generic lifecycle logic, `shared/map/live-map.ts`'s move out of `features/live/`) — the replay cockpit's own per-device telemetry panels need the identical per-device split `asset-detail.ts` already had, and this codebase has no precedent for one page importing another page's module. Both functions moved into `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts` (a natural home — it already held `deriveTrail`/`ageSeconds`/`isStale`, the same "sample-shape derivation" family); `asset-detail-logic.ts` re-exports them so its own import site (`asset-detail.ts`) needed zero changes, and its own spec file (`asset-detail-logic.spec.ts`) was trimmed to just `freshestSample`'s coverage (unchanged behavior) while the two relocated `describe` blocks landed, as-is, in `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.spec.ts` — the exact "relocated as-is, not new tests" idiom `core/fleet/warehouse-logic.spec.ts`'s own history entry already documents.

**Scrub/playback, concretely**: `ReplayPage.load()` fetches `getAsset(assetId)` and `usageTimeline(usageId, {maxPoints: 2000})` (the server's own clamp ceiling — R-a's `UsageTimelineController` docs) exactly once per route activation, no poller. Every panel is a `computed()` over that cached `timeline` signal and an `atMs` scrub signal: `trailPrefix`/`nearestSample` (map trail + marker, `O(log n)` binary search per call) and `bucketDetections`/`nearestDetectionResult`/`isDetectionNear` (the density strip + "what's showing now" panel) — dragging the `<input type="range">` scrub bar only calls `atMs.set(...)`, never HTTP, so it's exactly as smooth as any other signal-driven re-render regardless of flight length. Playback advances `atMs` via `requestAnimationFrame` (not `PollScheduler` — mirrors `shared/player/player.ts`'s own precedent of a raw timer for a single view's playback clock, see Gotchas), calling the pure `advancePlaybackClock(atMs, deltaRealMs, speed, fromMs, toMs)` each frame; reaching `toMs` stops playback rather than looping (a referee reviewing a specific moment wants playback to land and stay, not silently restart), and the Play button relabels **Replay** once at the end. A speed change (1×/4×/16×) needs no special-cased transition — `speed` is read fresh every tick, so the very next frame just advances by a different multiplier.

**Open usages are out of scope by design**: the history row shows Replay only for `endedAt`-carrying usages (an open one shows **Watch live** instead, `/live/:deviceId`); a direct link to an open usage's replay URL still resolves (the endpoint itself works fine — `to` just defaults to "now"), but `ReplayPage` shows a redirect notice rather than the cockpit, since scrubbing a window that's still growing underneath the bar isn't the reviewed-flight experience this feature is for.

**Detections' three honest empty states**, never collapsed into one generic dash: **"No detections recorded for this flight"** (`timeline.detections` is empty outright — a legacy usage from before R-a2's `AssetUsage.streamId` link, or a streamless asset, per R-a's own documented gap), **"No detection data near this moment"** (detections exist elsewhere in the flight, but the nearest one is further than `DETECTION_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS` = 2s from the scrub position — e.g. CV only ran intermittently), and **"Nothing detected at this instant"** (the nearest inference frame ran, right near the scrub time, and simply saw nothing). The density strip only marks *positive* frames (`detections.length > 0`) — an analyzed-but-empty frame is not "where a detection occurred".

**Test count: 288 → 320** (32 new — verified: 288 + 32 = 320, matches exactly):
- `features/replay/replay-logic.spec.ts` — 30 cases: `nearestSample` (7, incl. exact match, tie-breaking toward the earlier sample, before/after-range clamping), `trailPrefix` (4), `nearestDetectionResult` (2, incl. resolving to a zero-detection result as the honest nearest answer), `isDetectionNear` (3, incl. the exact tolerance boundary), `bucketDetections` (6, incl. merging close results into one bucket and clamping an out-of-range `capturedAt` into the first/last bucket rather than dropping it), `clampToRange` (2), `advancePlaybackClock` (6, incl. a same-`deltaRealMs`-different-`speed` comparison proving the "no special case for speed changes" claim, end-of-range stop, and starting already-at-`toMs`).
- `core/api/vision-api.spec.ts` — 2 new cases (`usageTimeline`: no query params by default; `fromMs`/`toMs`/`maxPoints` passed through when given).
- `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.spec.ts` — 4 cases for `groupTelemetryByDevice`/`telemetryDevices`, relocated as-is from `asset-detail-logic.spec.ts` (not new — the functions moved, the coverage came with them; net test count is therefore unaffected by the move itself, only by the 32 genuinely new cases above).
- No page-component-level specs for `replay.ts`/`replay-map.ts` — consistent with this app's existing precedent (every prior UI cycle's own Status entry makes the same call, most recently U3's); exercised by the full production build (twice, from clean, AOT `strictTemplates: true` — catches template-binding type errors) and close pattern-matching against `shared/map/live-map.ts`'s already-shipped Leaflet lifecycle code, which `replay-map.ts` mirrors near-verbatim. **Deviation, honestly noted**: no live-stack visual screenshot was taken (the frontend-design skill's own "screenshot and critique" guidance) — doing so needs a booted backend with a finished, telemetry-and-detection-bearing usage seeded, which was judged out of proportion to this cycle's time budget; the CSS reuses `asset-detail.css`'s own already-shipped, visually-verified classes (`.facts`/`.telemetry-grid`/`.detail-grid`/skeleton) nearly verbatim rather than inventing new layout, which is the mitigation for that gap.

**Bundle sizes** (`ng build --configuration production`, before → after; before = U3's own recorded "after" numbers above, i.e. the working state this cycle started from):
- **Initial total: 301.91 kB raw / 83.94 kB transfer → 302.58 kB raw / 84.41 kB transfer (+0.67 kB raw / +0.47 kB transfer)** — **a correction to the task brief's "don't grow it", found while measuring, not aimed for.** Every one of replay's own new modules (`features/replay/**`, `ReplayMap`) is reachable only from the new lazy `replay` chunk — confirmed zero-eager the same way U3's own entry did (grep for the new symbols in the initial chunks finds nothing). The entire delta is `VisionApi.usageTimeline()` — one new method's own minified body — landing in the initial bundle because `VisionApi` is `providedIn: 'root'` and already eagerly loaded by the shell; this is the identical, unavoidable cost every past cycle that added a `VisionApi`/`FleetStore` method also paid (CW-b's 8 new methods cost ~2.9 kB, C4's 2 new methods cost ~0.9 kB) — `models.ts`'s new `UsageTimeline` type itself costs nothing (types erase). Avoiding it would mean either not adding a typed `VisionApi` method (breaking this file's own "no component calls `fetch` directly" convention, carved out today only for the Debug console) or leaving `usageTimeline` unused by a real page — neither was judged an acceptable trade for ~0.67 kB. The bundle stays 2.58 kB over the pre-existing 300 kB **warning** threshold (was already 1.91 kB over it after U2's CDK addition; nowhere close to the 360 kB **error** one) — the same "flagged, not hidden" posture U2's own Status entry set for its own threshold crossing.
- **New `replay` chunk: 19.52 kB raw / 5.94 kB transfer** — the whole cockpit (page + map sub-component + all the scrub/playback/detection logic), comparable to `map`'s own 21.95/6.43 and smaller than `asset-detail`'s 25.20/6.63 despite being an entirely new surface, since it reuses `shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts` rather than rebuilding any map bootstrap.
- **`asset-detail`: 24.80 kB / 6.52 kB → 25.20 kB / 6.63 kB** (+0.40 kB / +0.11 kB — the usage history table's new Replay/Watch-live column + `RouterLink` bindings; `groupTelemetryByDevice`/`telemetryDevices` moving to `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts` costs this chunk nothing net, since it already imported them from `asset-detail-logic.ts`'s now-thinner re-export).
- **`leaflet-src`: unchanged at 149.55 kB / 37.58 kB** — `ReplayMap` reuses `shared/map/leaflet-loader.ts#importLeaflet()` exactly like every other map; no new Leaflet APIs, confirming "leaflet stays shared" held.
- **`devices`/`map`/`live`/`wall`/`debug`/`settings`/`hls`: unchanged (± ~40 bytes of esbuild minification noise on `devices`, not attributable to any changed source in this cycle)** — none of their source changed; verified by diffing against U3's own recorded numbers.

**Deviations from the task brief, with reasons**:
- **Initial bundle grew by 0.67 kB, not "stayed at 301.91 kB" as the brief asked** — see the Bundle sizes entry above for the full accounting; the growth is `VisionApi.usageTimeline()`'s own code, not anything replay-specific leaking eager, and is proportionate to every past cycle's own "new `VisionApi` method costs a few hundred bytes to a few kB" experience.
- **`groupTelemetryByDevice`/`telemetryDevices` moved to `core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts`** — not called out in the task brief's own literal text, but a direct, previously-established consequence of "reuse/extend existing telemetry formatting logic" once a second page needed the identical per-device split; see the dedicated writeup above.
- **No dedicated `ReplayMap`/`ReplayPage` component-level tests** — consistent with, not a departure from, this app's own established precedent (every map/page component in this codebase ships without one; only the pure logic underneath is unit-tested) — see the Test count entry above for the honest gap this leaves (no live-stack screenshot) and its mitigation.
- **`AssetDetailPage.assetId`'s route-param mismatch, found but not fixed** — out of R-b's own scope (it's `asset-detail.ts`, not `replay.ts`); flagged in Gotchas instead, with the replay route's own params deliberately named to not repeat it.
