## U-d — Asset & warehouse rework: frontend half (docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-d)

A backend agent built the pinned contract this batch (`POST /api/devices/probe`; `PUT/GET/DELETE
/api/assets/{id}/image`; `PATCH /api/assets/{id}` attributes) concurrently — coded against verbatim
per that task's own "code defensively" instruction; this section's own "Live-verification" list at
the end names exactly what a live restart against the finished backend should confirm.

### New feature: `features/onboarding/**` — the wizard

**Route**: `/add-source` (`onboarding.routes.ts`, own lazy chunk — 52.73 kB raw / 13.62 kB transfer,
see Bundle impact below), replacing the inline "+ Add source" card the Devices page used to open on
itself. Reached from Warehouse's own "+ Add source" button (`DevicesPage#goToAddSource`) and from
Fly's pre-existing `/devices?addSource=1` empty-state link, which now redirects straight through
(`DevicesPage`'s constructor still reads the `addSource` query-param input, but navigates to
`/add-source` instead of opening a card — Fly's own link, out of this task's scope, needed no edit).

**Architecture** — four pieces, each with one job, mirroring how every other page/store pair in this
app is split:

- `onboarding.ts`/`.html`/`.css` — `OnboardingPage`, a thin `@switch (store.step())` shell: one
  section per step, a Back/Next footer, nothing else. `providers: [OnboardingStore]` scopes a fresh
  store instance to this route, the same DI-sharing idiom `AssetDetailPage` already uses for
  `TelemetryStore`/`DetectionsStore` — a second pass through the wizard never starts warm with a
  previous attempt's half-filled form.
- `onboarding-store.ts` — `OnboardingStore`, the wizard's own "component store" the plan's own
  wording asked for: every signal across all four steps, plus the actual HTTP orchestration
  (`probe()`, `scan()`, `createAsset()`, …). Deliberately thin glue — every yes/no decision and every
  request shape is delegated to `onboarding-logic.ts`, exactly like `features/devices/devices.ts`'s
  own pre-existing relationship with `devices-page-logic.ts`.
- `onboarding-logic.ts` — pure, Angular-free: the step-machine (`nextStep`/`prevStep`, `WizardStep`/
  `ConnectMethod` types), the poka-yoke advance gates (`canAdvanceFromProfile`/`canAdvanceFromConnect`/
  `canAdvanceFromTest`), and the request builders (`buildProbeRequest`/`buildCreateAssetRequest`/
  `buildPostSimulationAssetEdit`). Fully unit-tested (`onboarding-logic.spec.ts`) with no HTTP, no
  router, no DOM at all.
- `image-downscale.ts` — the Profile step's photo pipeline, split pure/DOM per its own doc comment:
  `computeTargetDimensions`/`isAcceptableImageType`/`JPEG_QUALITY_STEPS` are pure and tested
  (`image-downscale.spec.ts`); `downscaleImageToJpeg` draws into a real `<canvas>` (`createImageBitmap`
  when available, an `HTMLImageElement`+`Image.onload` fallback otherwise) and tries
  `JPEG_QUALITY_STEPS` (0.92 → 0.35) until the encoded `Blob` clears `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` (2MB, the
  pinned `PUT /api/assets/{id}/image` limit) or the ladder runs out (best effort at the lowest step —
  the `PUT` itself is the final, authoritative check). jsdom (this app's test env) has no canvas, so
  this half is exercised only by hand — see Live-verification below.
- `protocols.ts` (+ its own spec) moved here **verbatim, unchanged**, from `features/devices/` — the
  Register method's protocol `<select>` (`REGISTERABLE_PROTOCOLS`/`CUSTOM_PROTOCOL_OPTION`/
  `placeholderForProtocol`/`protocolSelectionFor`) is now onboarding-only; the Warehouse page never
  rendered this select at all, only `Device.protocol` as a plain chip.

### The 4 steps

1. **Profile** — display name, registration/tail number (optional, the `registrationNumber`
   attributes-key convention — see `core/fleet/asset-attributes.ts` below), photo upload with preview
   (canvas downscale, see above), category picker (`core/fleet/category-logic.ts`, moved from
   `features/devices/devices-page-logic.ts` — see below).
2. **Connect** — the pre-existing register/discover/simulate 3-choice component, **moved wholesale**
   out of `features/devices/devices.ts` into `OnboardingStore`, preserving every field and behavior
   byte-for-byte: the protocol `<select>` + `Custom…` escape hatch + advanced-mode stream options,
   the discovery scan + "Use" candidate-fill, and all four simulate modes (`direct`/`rtsp`/
   `testDrone`/`synthetic`) including the flight-plan dialog integration (`shared/map/flight-plan-dialog.ts`,
   imported read-only — that module's own doc comment is now one line stale, "the Devices page's
   Add-source Simulate step"; not fixed here, `shared/map/**` is a different concurrent agent's scope
   this batch, flagged below). One behavioral simplification: the old page's `scrollIntoView`+
   outline-highlight hack for "Use" (needed because the register form and the discovery table shared
   one crowded page) is gone — the wizard's own step transition (discover → register sub-view) *is*
   the affordance now, so nothing was lost, just no longer needed.
3. **Test** — `POST /api/devices/probe` (UX-DESIGN §5.1 "test-before-save"): the decoded frame, WxH/
   codec/fps/telemetry-detected facts, warnings, a Retry button, and the specific error text the
   backend's own `ApiErrorBody.message` supplies verbatim (`describeHttpError`'s existing default
   branch already surfaces any non-500 server message, 422 included — no new case needed there).
   **Poka-yoke**: `OnboardingStore#canAdvanceTest` requires the *last successful probe* to still match
   the *current* protocol/URI/options (`probeStillCurrent`, a `computed` diffing the last-probed
   request against the live one) — editing the connection after a successful probe silently
   re-disables Next until it's re-tested, not just "the first probe ever succeeded". **Skipped
   entirely for Simulate** (`nextStep('connect', 'simulate')` → `'create'` directly) — starting the
   simulation *is* the proof it works; there is no separate device to probe ahead of it.
4. **Create** — a summary, then the actual persistence call:
   - **Register/Discover**: **one** `POST /api/assets` call, `CreateAssetRequest.devices[0]`
     embedding the connection as a `CreateAssetDeviceSpec` (name = the asset's own display name — this
     wizard has no separate device-naming field anywhere in it, on purpose: it thinks in assets, not
     devices). This is what closes docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-d item 2's "orphaned-device dead end" —
     no device is ever registered on its own, unowned.
   - **Simulate, `direct`/`rtsp`/`testDrone`**: `POST /api/simulations` "as today"
     (`fleet.simulate()`, so the device/stream lists refresh and a failure is toasted exactly like
     every other simulate call site), then a follow-up `PATCH /api/assets/{id}` applies
     name/`registrationNumber` if either was given (`buildPostSimulationAssetEdit`) — the simulation
     endpoint has no `attributes`/custom-name-at-create-time shape of its own.
   - **Simulate, `synthetic`** — **a deliberate deviation from "as today", flagged for review**: the
     pre-wizard "Add the simulated source" quick-add (`buildSyntheticRegisterRequest`) registered a
     bare `sim`/`sim://demo` **device**, with no owning asset at all — itself an orphaned-device dead
     end, just a zero-hardware one. Perpetuating that *inside the very wizard whose stated job is
     closing that gap* was judged inconsistent, so `synthetic` is instead routed through the **same**
     `POST /api/assets` call as Register/Discover, using `buildSyntheticRegisterRequest`'s own
     `protocol`/`uri` output as the embedded device's connection. `features/devices/devices.ts`'s own
     empty-state "Add the simulated source" one-click quick-add is **unchanged** — still the old
     orphaning quick-add, deliberately, since it predates this wizard, isn't part of the 3-choice
     component, and is out of this specific plan item's stated scope; flagged in case a future cycle
     wants it closed too.
   - **Photo**, if one was chosen, is applied via `PUT /api/assets/{id}/image` after the asset exists,
     on every path above — a soft failure here (`applyPhotoIfAny`/`finishCreate`'s own try/catch)
     still lets the asset creation itself succeed, with its own toast naming the photo failure
     separately, never silently swallowed.
   - Every path ends the same way: `fleet.refresh({quiet:true})` (Warehouse sees the new asset/device
     immediately on the next visit), a success toast, then `router.navigate(['/assets', assetId])`.

### Shared logic promoted to `core/` (the established "second consumer → `core/`" rule)

Three pieces moved out of `features/devices/**`'s own private modules once the wizard became a
second consumer — the exact same rule `core/fleet/device-logic.ts`/`core/fleet/warehouse-logic.ts`

  `features/devices/simulate-logic.ts` keeps only the Warehouse-only display concern that was never

- **`core/fleet/category-logic.ts`** (new file) absorbed `CategoryOption`/`DEFAULT_CATEGORY_OPTIONS`/

  step and Warehouse's own "Promote to asset…" panel need the identical "existing categories +
  fallback list" picker. `devices-page-logic.ts` re-exports everything from here (mirrors its own
  pre-existing `warehouse-logic.ts` re-export block) so its own import site needed no changes.
- **`core/fleet/asset-attributes.ts`** (new file) — the `registrationNumber` attributes-key
  convention: `REGISTRATION_NUMBER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY`, `registrationNumberOf`, `withRegistrationNumber`
  (create/set), `withoutRegistrationNumber` (explicit clear — see its own doc comment for why a
  *create* flow and an *edit* flow need different blank-input behavior). Shared by the wizard's
  Create step and the asset detail page's inline edit — the one convention both need to agree on.

### Warehouse rename (docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-d item 4)

`features/devices/**` is now "the Warehouse" everywhere a person reads it, while staying `/devices`
everywhere a machine reads it:

- **Page**: `<h1>Warehouse</h1>`, updated intro copy; nav tab label `app.ts`'s `tabs` array: `'Assets'`

### `features/asset-detail/**` additions (docs/UX-REWORK-PLAN.md §U-d item 3)

- **Photo**: `assetImageSrc` (a `computed`) binds `<img [src]>` to `api.assetImageUrl(assetId)` only
  when `asset()?.hasImage` is true and the fetch hasn't already 404'd this page-view
  (`imageLoadFailed`, an `(error)` handler on the `<img>` itself — reset only when `assetId()` changes
  via the routing effect, deliberately *not* on every 5s poll tick, or a genuine 404 would flicker
  retry-then-fail every poll cycle forever). Rendered next to the header's name/chips.
- **Registration/tail number**: `registrationNumber` (a `computed` off `registrationNumberOf`) in the
  Characteristics card, with an inline edit (`editingRegistrationNumber`/`registrationNumberDraft`) —
  `confirmEditRegistrationNumber` always starts from the asset's **complete current** `attributes`
  map before adding/removing the one key (see the "full replacement, not a merge" note below), and
  blanking the field to empty explicitly *removes* the key (`withoutRegistrationNumber`), not "leave
  the old value alone" the way the wizard's own create-time `withRegistrationNumber` behaves.
- **Attributes editor**: gated behind `settings.advancedMode()` — raw key/value rows
  (`attributeRows`/`addAttributeRow`/`removeAttributeRow`/`updateAttributeKey`/`updateAttributeValue`),
  seeded from `attributesToRows(asset.attributes)` on open, submitted as
  `attributeRowsToRecord(attributeRows())` on Save (both pure, `asset-detail-logic.ts`, tested). Shows
  every attribute raw, `registrationNumber` included — it's the escape hatch, not a second,
  inconsistent view of the same data.
- **Verified against the actual backend source, not assumed**: `PATCH /api/assets/{id}`'s
  `attributes` field is a **full replacement map, never a merge**
  (`vision-application/.../AssetEdit.java`'s own Javadoc: "replacement attributes, or `null` to keep
  the current map" — read directly before writing either editor). Both editors above are careful to
  always build their submitted map from the asset's **complete** current `attributes`, never a
  partial delta — sending just `{registrationNumber: "…"}` would silently wipe out every other
  attribute the asset had.

## F-d — flight-controller-aware telemetry UI (docs/FC-INTEGRATIONS-PLAN.md F-d)

Built against the plan's own **frozen wire contract** ahead of/alongside the backend half
(F-a/F-b/F-c, other agents, `vision-domain`/`adapters/adapter-mavlink`/`vision-application`/
`vision-api`/`adapters/adapter-persistence`/`adapters/adapter-simulation` — outside this module's own
scope, not touched here) — delivers the frontend half of Tier-1's "RTH/failsafe banners" and
"telemetry-verified pre-flight checklist" over the existing telemetry pipe (`TelemetrySample`'s new
`flightState?`/`extra?`, `AssetAttention`'s new `flightMode?`/`armed?`/`failsafe?` — see the API
surface section above for the exact wire shapes).

**New**: `core/telemetry/flight-state-logic.ts` (+`.spec.ts`, 34 cases — see its own bullet above in
API surface/core for the full function list: `gpsFixLabel`/`gpsSeverity`/`flightBanner`/
`derivePreflight`), `features/fly/failsafe-banner.ts` (`<vision-failsafe-banner>`), `features/fly/preflight-checklist.ts`
(`<vision-preflight-checklist>`).

- **`features/fly/failsafe-banner.ts`** — a full-width strip laid over the video
  (`fly.html`'s new `.hud.hud-banner`, `z-index: 10` — above the ordinary HUD layer's `6` but below
  the two modals' `20`), kind-dependent class (`banner-failsafe` → `--live` red; `banner-rth`/
  `banner-landing` → `--warn` amber), B612 Mono uppercase. Deliberately dumb: one input
  (`banner: FlightBanner | null`), computed once in `fly.ts` (`failsafeBanner = computed(() =>
  flightBanner(telemetry.latest()))`) and passed straight through — the component owns no
  telemetry access of its own. **Geometric shift, not a z-index chase** (mirrors `.hud-map`'s own
  "BROKEN #1" fix, Gotchas above): `fly.css`'s `.cockpit.banner-active` class (bound to
  `failsafeBanner() !== null`) shifts `.hud-header`/`.hud-osd`/`.hud-map`/`.hud-ticker` down by the
  banner's own fixed `min-height: 2.2rem` rather than letting the banner paint over (and block
  clicks on) the header's own controls.
- **`features/fly/preflight-checklist.ts`** — a compact card (`✓`/`✕`/`—` glyphs, severity-colored)
  listing `derivePreflight`'s 5 rows verbatim, arming blockers rendered under the Armable row exactly
  as the FC reported them (`^(PreArm|Arm): …`, never paraphrased). Shown (`fly.html`'s new
  `.hud.hud-preflight`, bottom-left, clear of both `.hud-controls` and `.hud-secondary`) only when
  `!watchMode() && (telemetry.latest() === undefined || latest.flightState?.armed !== true)` — a
  ground-check card, gone once the FC confirms armed (the OSD chip bar is the live instrument from
  that point on).
- **`features/fly/fly-osd.ts`** — 5 new chips, each independently omitted (never fabricated) when its
  own field is absent: **ground speed** (`extra['groundspeedMps']`, one decimal, `X.Xm/s` — closes
  this component's own previously-documented "no speed reading" gap, doc comment rewritten in place
  rather than left stale), **mode** (`flightState.mode`, plain text), **GPS** (`gpsFixLabel` +
  satellite count, e.g. `"3D · 12 sat"`, colored by `gpsSeverity`), **armed/disarmed** (armed: mild
  green-ish, matching no other severity tier so it doesn't compete with `--live`/`--danger`;
  disarmed: dimmed via `opacity`, not colored — a grounded drone is the normal state, not a flag),
  **RSSI** (`rssiPercent` + `%`, plain chip, no severity tier — the plan didn't call for one and none
  of this app's other raw-signal readouts invents a threshold without a documented one).
- **`features/command/command-logic.ts`** — `AttentionReasonKind` gains **`failsafe`** (new top rank,
  above `battery-critical` — `REASON_RANK` renumbered `failsafe:6 … open-events:1`, kept internally
  consistent, not just appended) and **`gps-degraded`** (ranked between `battery-low` and
  `open-events`). `failsafeReason(asset)` fires only on `asset.failsafe === true` (never fabricated
  from `undefined`/`false`); `gpsDegradedReason(gpsFixType)` takes `gpsFixType` as an explicit
  parameter — **not** read off `AssetAttention` (the fleet-summary DTO doesn't carry GPS quality, see
  that interface's own doc comment) — reusing `flight-state-logic.ts#gpsSeverity` rather than
  re-deriving the tiers. `attentionReasons`/`buildEntityRows` both gained an optional trailing
  parameter (`gpsFixType?`/`gpsFixTypeByAssetId?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>`) so every existing call
  site (`asset-panel.ts`) keeps compiling unchanged; `command.ts`'s own `entityRows` computed now
  builds that map from `mapStore.markers()` (`FleetMarker.gpsFixType`) and threads it through — an
  asset with no live marker simply never triggers that one reason, the same "unknown, not fabricated"
  posture as everywhere else in this module.
- **`core/map/map-logic.ts#FleetMarker`** gained `flightMode?`/`armed?`/`failsafe?`/`gpsFixType?`,
  sourced in `buildMarker` from the streaming asset's own latest telemetry sample's `flightState` —
  the same place `headingDegrees`/`batteryPercent` already come from, **not** `AssetSummary`
  (`buildMarker`'s own input, which carries none of this) and deliberately a *different* derivation
  from `AssetAttention`'s own `flightMode`/`armed`/`failsafe` (fleet-summary-level; see that
  interface's doc comment) — this marker-level set exists for `shared/map/fleet-map/fleet-map.ts`'s
  popup and `features/command/asset-panel.ts`'s Status tab, both of which only ever have a
  `FleetMarker` in hand. Absent entirely for the `offline` bucket (no live telemetry poller).
- **`features/command/asset-panel.ts`/`.html`** — Status tab gained Mode/Armed/GPS facts, preferring
  the live `marker()` (fresher) and falling back to the fleet-summary `asset()` fields for
  Mode/Armed (GPS has no such fallback — marker-only, `AssetAttention` doesn't carry it); Armed
  renders as plain text (`'Armed'`/`'Disarmed'`/`'—'`), deliberately uncolored — armed isn't itself a
  severity. GPS text colors `.gps-warn-text`/`.gps-critical-text` (new, `asset-panel.css`) rather than
  reusing the existing `.stale-text` (red-only) — one primary signal color per severity tier, amber
  vs. red kept distinct. `reasons` now threads `marker()?.gpsFixType` into `attentionReasons`.
- **`features/command/command.html`/`.css`** — rail row gained a compact **`FS`** chip
  (`.fs-chip`, `--live` red via `color-mix`, this app's existing precedent for a translucent tinted
  background — `app.css`) shown when `row.asset.failsafe === true`, distinct from the generic
  `.severity-chip` (`--danger`-based) so a genuine failsafe always reads as more urgent than any other
  critical reason at a glance.
- **`features/wall/wall-tile.ts`** — a small uppercase mode badge in the tile footer
  (`.mode-chip`, plain neutral by default), red (`--live`) when `flightState.failsafe === true`;
  omitted entirely with no `flightState` yet (a device with no MAVLink-carrying telemetry link still
  shows nothing, never a fabricated "—" badge cluttering every tile).
- **`shared/map/fleet-map/fleet-map.ts`** — popup gained a `Mode …` line when `marker.flightMode` is
  present, inline-styled `--live` red + bold when `marker.failsafe === true` (Leaflet popups are raw
  HTML strings, not Angular templates — a CSS class defined in this component's own `fleet-map.css`
  wouldn't reach it any more directly than the inline style does; `escapeHtml` still guards the mode
  string like every other user-controlled popup field here).

**Poka-yoke, verified across every piece above**: no fake data anywhere — every absent field renders
`'—'`/no chip/no row, never a fabricated `'ok'`/green tick; `--live` red is used *only* for a genuine
failsafe (never a generic "critical" severity, which stays on `--danger`); banners/badges state what
the *aircraft* is doing (`'FAILSAFE — RETURNING TO HOME'`), never an instruction to the operator.

## I-b "Listen for drones" onboarding + F-e ArduPilot diagnostics surfaces (docs/DRONE-INFRA-PLAN.md I-b, docs/FC-INTEGRATIONS-PLAN.md F-e)

Both built against each plan's own frozen contract while the backend halves (`MavlinkHeartbeatScanner`
in `adapter-mavlink`, F-e's `WIND`/`VIBRATION`/`EKF_STATUS_REPORT`/`RANGEFINDER`/`MISSION_CURRENT`
decode) landed concurrently in the same working tree — **the actual landed backend code was read
afterward, read-only, to verify this frontend's own assumptions against it** (not to write against
it directly; this module's file scope stayed `vision-web/**` only): `MavlinkHeartbeatScanner#toDiscoveredDevice`
confirms the exact `details` map shape this task assumed (`details["firmware"]` — literal `"unknown"`
string, never absent; `details["mavType"]`; `details["sysid"]`; `details["claimed"] = "true"` +
`details["claimedBy"]` only once a vehicle is claimed) and the exact name format
(`"ArduPilot quadcopter (sysid 7)"`) — both match this section's own `drone-scan-logic.ts` below
verbatim, no rework needed. One wire-shape subtlety worth recording: `StreamDescriptor.options`
(the domain-level `sysid` pin) is **not** flattened by `dto.DiscoveredDeviceResponse` — that DTO
only ever flattens `protocol`/`uri` from `suggestedStream`, never its `options` map (verified by
reading `DiscoveredDeviceResponse.java`, unmodified by either concurrent backend task) — which is
exactly why the backend redundantly duplicates the sysid into `details["sysid"]` too, and why
`drone-scan-logic.ts#prefillFromVehicle` reads it from there rather than expecting it on
`DiscoveredDevice` directly.

### Part 1 — I-b: `features/onboarding/**`'s fourth Connect-step tile

- **New `features/onboarding/drone-scan-logic.ts`** (+`.spec.ts`, 18 cases) — pure, Angular-free,
  mirrors `onboarding-logic.ts`'s own split: `MAVLINK_DISCOVERY_METHOD` (`"mavlink"`),
  `buildMavlinkScanRequest(timeoutMs?)` (→ `ScanRequest` restricted to `methods: ['mavlink']`; no
  `timeoutMs` sent unless given — the scanner self-time-boxes ~5-10s, so unlike the general
  "Discover on network" method there is no timeout picker for this one), `isClaimedVehicle`
  (`details['claimed'] === 'true'`), `vehicleSysid` (`details['sysid']`), `vehicleDetailChips`
  (firmware + sysid only — a deliberately narrower pair than the general Discover table's
  generic `detailPairs` dump of every `details` entry, per the plan's own "details chips (firmware,
  sysid)" wording; `mavType`/`claimedBy` ride in `details` unused by this UI), and
  `prefillFromVehicle` (→ protocol/uri/`{sysid}` options/`suggestedCategory`, falling back to
  `"mavlink"`/`candidate.address` the same way `useCandidate` already falls back for the general
  Discover path). `ScanRequest.methods`/`DiscoveredDevice.details` already existed in `models.ts`
  pre-task (no wire-model change needed) — verified before writing any of the above, not assumed.
- **`onboarding-logic.ts`**: `ConnectMethod` gains a fourth member, `'listen'` — behaves exactly like
  `'discover'` in every existing gate (`canAdvanceFromConnect`'s `'listen'` case returns `false`,
  same as `'discover'`; `nextStep`/`prevStep` needed no change at all, since their own `method ===
  'simulate' ? … : …` ternary already treats every non-simulate method identically). Picking an
  unclaimed vehicle flips the method to `'register'` with the form prefilled — the same
  "candidate → register" pivot `'discover'`'s own "Use" button already uses, not a new step-machine
  state. 3 new `onboarding-logic.spec.ts` cases cover the `'listen'` variant through
  `nextStep`/`canAdvanceFromConnect`/`canAdvanceFromTest`.
- **`onboarding-store.ts`**: `droneScanning`/`droneScanResult` signals + `scanForDrones()` (calls
  `api.scan(buildMavlinkScanRequest())`, no timeout picker) + `useDroneVehicle(candidate)` (a
  no-op for an already-claimed candidate — defensive, since the UI never offers the action for one
  anyway; otherwise mirrors `useCandidate` plus filling `category` from `suggestedCategory` when the
  Profile step's own category field is still blank — this is the one path in this wizard that closes
  the previously-documented "discovery's `suggestedCategory` isn't wired into the Profile step's
  category picker" Gotcha, for `listen` specifically, not the general `discover` method).
- **`onboarding.ts`/`.html`/`.css`**: a fourth `.method-tile` ("Listen for drones", its own
  `.glyph-listen` — concentric rings, distinct from `.glyph-discover`'s dashed ring) alongside the
  original three; a new `@case ('listen')` results view — one `<li class="vehicle-row">` per heard
  vehicle (name, `vehicleDetailChips`' firmware/sysid chips, a `Use` button), **not** the general
  Discover method's `<table>` (fewer columns fit this scan's narrower "drone only" purpose better);
  a claimed vehicle renders `.vehicle-row.claimed` (dimmed, `opacity: 0.6`) with `Use` disabled and
  an inline `.disabled-reason` "Already registered" (the U-a2 poka-yoke idiom this app already uses
  everywhere else a disabled control needs its reason told inline, not just in a tooltip) — never
  hidden, so the scan's own "it heard this vehicle" proof stays visible. Empty scan (`result.devices
  .length === 0`): "No drones heard on UDP 14550 — check the link recipes in infra/edge/." + a
  rescan button, per the plan's own exact wording. Loading state mirrors the wizard's existing style
  (`store.droneScanning()` → "Listening…" button label + an `.empty`/`.faint` "Listening for
  heartbeats…" placeholder, same idiom as every other async step in this wizard). "Allow
  cancel-by-navigation" needed no explicit `AbortController`: leaving `/add-source` destroys the
  per-route-provided `OnboardingStore` (`providers: [OnboardingStore]` on `OnboardingPage`), so an
  in-flight scan's eventual response simply has nowhere left to land.
- **`CONNECT_METHOD_LABELS`**/`connectionSummary`'s exhaustive switches both gained the `'listen'`
  case (label `'Listen for drones'`; summary groups with `'register'`/`'discover'` — in practice
  never reached, since picking a vehicle always flips the method to `'register'` first, identical
  to how `'discover'`'s own case in that switch is already unreachable in practice).

### Part 2 — F-e: diagnostics rows, reused by Fly and Command

- **New `core/telemetry/flight-state-logic.ts` additions** (+22 new spec cases, same file/spec
  `F-d` already owns — no new file, this is a natural extension of the existing flight-state pure
  logic): `ekfSeverity(variance)` (ok `< 0.5`, warn `0.5–1.0` inclusive, bad `> 1.0`),
  `vibeSeverity(ms2)` (ok `< 30`, warn `30–60` inclusive, bad `> 60`), `DiagnosticRow`/
  `DiagnosticSeverity` types, and `deriveDiagnostics(extra: Record<string, number> | undefined)` —
  **takes the raw `extra` map directly, not a whole `TelemetrySample`**, specifically so both
  consumers below can feed it whatever `extra` they actually have in hand (a live sample's own
  `extra` for Fly, a `FleetMarker`'s passed-through `extra` for Command) without either one needing
  a second telemetry poller. Five possible rows, fixed order, each independently omitted (not
  present with a fabricated value) when its own frozen `extra` key(s) are absent: **wind**
  (`windSpeedMps` + optional `windDirectionDegrees`, no severity — F-e defines none), **vibration**
  (any of `vibeXMs2`/`vibeYMs2`/`vibeZMs2` present; only the present axes are shown, the *worst*
  one's own value governs the row's severity), **EKF** (any of `ekfVelocityVariance`/
  `ekfPosHorizVariance`/`ekfPosVertVariance`/`ekfCompassVariance`; the worst one governs both the
  severity and which one is named in the value string, e.g. `"compass 1.23"` — never averaged,
  never silently picking the first one present), **rangefinder** (`rangefinderDistanceM`, no
  severity), **mission** (`missionSeq` → `"Waypoint <n>"`, no severity).
- **`core/map/map-logic.ts#FleetMarker`** gained `extra?: Record<string, number>`, sourced in
  `buildMarker` from the same latest-sample the existing `flightMode`/`armed`/etc. fields already
  read (`latest?.extra`, verbatim passthrough — no new derivation) — this is what lets
  `asset-panel.ts`'s Status tab call `deriveDiagnostics` without a second `TelemetryStore` poller,
  the identical reuse rationale F-d's own `flightMode`/`armed`/`failsafe`/`gpsFixType` additions
  already established for this interface. Absent entirely for the `offline` bucket, same rule as
  every other live-telemetry-sourced field here. 3 new `map-logic.spec.ts` cases.
- **`features/fly/diagnostics-card.ts`** (new, `<vision-diagnostics-card>`) — a compact,
  collapsible HUD card (own internal `expanded` signal, default open; a header button toggles it),
  `rows: readonly DiagnosticRow[]` its only input, deliberately dumb like `FailsafeBanner`/
  `PreflightChecklist` — issues no HTTP, holds no store. Hidden entirely with no rows, via the same
  belt-and-suspenders double-guard `FailsafeBanner` already uses (an internal `@if (rows().length >
  0)` *and* `fly.html`'s own `@if (diagnosticsRows().length > 0)` around the `<vision-diagnostics-
  card>` tag). Severity colors reuse this app's existing tokens: plain default for `'ok'`/no-severity
  rows, `--warn` amber, `--danger` red — **never `--live`**, which this app reserves exclusively for
  a genuine failsafe (see `FailsafeBanner`'s own doc comment; F-e's own bad-vibration/bad-EKF rows
  are "attention", not "the aircraft is failsafing"). `fly.ts#diagnosticsRows = computed(() =>
  deriveDiagnostics(telemetry.latest()?.extra))`; `fly.html`'s new `.hud.hud-diagnostics` sits at
  `right: 0.75rem; bottom: 5.7rem` (`fly.css`) — the right-column mirror of `.hud-preflight`'s own
  fixed left-column offset above `.hud-controls`, clear of `.hud-detections` below and `.hud-map`
  above at this app's ≥1280px viewport floor (an approximate, not computed, offset — same caveat
  `.hud-preflight`'s own comment already carries).
- **`features/fly/fly-osd.ts`** gained a wind chip — `extra['windSpeedMps']` (one decimal, `X.Xm/s`)
  plus an arrow glyph (`➤`) rotated via an inline `[style.transform]="'rotate(' + deg + 'deg)'"` to
  `extra['windDirectionDegrees']` when that key is also present; the speed alone still renders
  without a direction. A second, compact rendering of the same wind data the Diagnostics card's own
  row shows — not a duplicate derivation, no severity tier (F-e defines none for wind).
- **`features/command/asset-panel.ts`/`.html`/`.css`** — Status tab's `dl.facts` gained the same
  `deriveDiagnostics` rows, appended after the existing Mode/Armed/GPS facts, fed from
  `marker()?.extra` (never a second poller — see `FleetMarker#extra`'s own doc comment above). New
  `.diag-warn-text`/`.diag-bad-text` CSS (`color: var(--warn)`/`var(--danger)`) rather than reusing
  `.gps-warn-text`/`.gps-critical-text` verbatim — those two are functionally identical color rules,
  but keeping a separate, non-GPS-named pair avoids a non-GPS row's class name reading as
  GPS-specific to a future reader.
- **No new component specs** for `DiagnosticsCard`/the onboarding wizard's `'listen'` sub-view —
  matches this codebase's own standing precedent (`FailsafeBanner`/`PreflightChecklist`/
  `AssetPanel`/`OnboardingPage` all have none either; only the pure `*-logic.ts` layer is
  unit-tested, component behavior is covered by the full production build + this doc's own
  description, per the established convention this file's own "Tests" sections have followed since
  U2).

## Q2/Q3 — ops quick wins: Undo toast, replay strip cap, composite box hues (docs/OPS-CORE-PLAN.md §Q)

Scope: `vision-web/**` only (Wave A, parallel with G-a/R-a's own Java-side work; Q1's event→replay
deep link is a later agent's — this batch left `features/replay/replay.ts`'s own structure alone
beyond the strip cap, and never touched `features/onboarding/**`/`core/telemetry/flight-state-logic.ts`).
No backend changes.

**Q2 — 10s Undo toast, closing U-a2 item 3b's own documented gap.** New `shared/ui/undo-toast.service.ts`/
`undo-toast.ts` (`UndoToastService`/`<vision-undo-toast>`) — see the API-surface bullet above (next to
`ToastService`) for the full shape: one toast at a time, 10s default, commit-on-replace/undo-only-cancels,
a CSS-animated progress bar, `Escape`-dismissable, mounted at the app root (`app.html`) **bottom-left**
(checked every existing `position: fixed`/`.hud-*` layout in the app first — `ToastHost` already owns
bottom-right, `features/fly/fly.css#.hud-controls` owns bottom-center at every supported viewport).
Wired into `features/devices/devices.ts`/`features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts`'s existing `archiveAssetNow`/
`archiveDeviceNow` (previously `ToastService.ok(text, {label:'Undo', onClick})`) **and** newly into
device `deactivate` via new `deactivateDeviceNow` methods on both pages (previously silent-immediacy —
a plain, action-less `FleetStore.setDeviceState` confirmation toast). `.danger-action` semantics
(the Archive button itself) are untouched — only what happens *after* the click changed. Asset-level
`activate`/`deactivate` are not reachable from any UI surface (U-a2 item 2 dropped them from every
operator-facing asset surface), so there was nothing to wire there; the explicit `restore`/`activate`
kebab entries are deliberately unchanged (re-activating isn't "silent immediacy" in the sense this item
means). `zone-delete` (the plan's third named flow) doesn't exist yet — G-c's zones UI lands in Wave B —
so `showUndo` is written generically enough for that agent to reuse verbatim, not wired to anything itself.

**Q3a — replay event strip cap.** `replay-logic.ts#capDetectionBuckets(buckets, cap = DETECTION_STRIP_CAP
= 200)` — a pure slice (no virtualization library) keeping only the latest 200 buckets plus the pre-cap
`totalCount`; `replay.ts` applies it over the existing `bucketDetections` output, and `replay.html` shows
a quiet "Showing latest N of totalCount markers" line under the scrub bar only when something was
actually trimmed. Rarely engages today — `DEFAULT_DETECTION_BUCKETS` (120) already sits under the 200
cap — kept as a real, tested backstop regardless rather than trusting bucket-count tuning alone forever.

**Q3b — composite box hues.** `shared/player/detection-overlay-logic.ts` gains `detectionModelKey(detection)`
(label-prefix extraction — deliberately not `Detection.modelId`, which is uniform across an entire
composite batch on the wire and so can't distinguish members within one; see that function's own doc
comment), `modelHue(modelKey, alphaPercent?)` (hash → hue, fixed saturation/lightness; `DEFAULT_MODEL_KEY`
always returns the byte-identical original box color, so a single-model stream — whichever model —
sees zero change), and `distinctModelKeys(detections)`. `shared/player/player.ts#drawBox` strokes/fills
every box via `modelHue` instead of the old hardcoded literals; a top-right legend chip (model → color
swatch) renders only once `showModelLegend` (≥2 distinct keys in the batch currently on screen,
`overlayResult`/`overlayModelKeys`) is true.

**Tests**: 854/854 → **884/884, 44 → 45 files** (+30: 11 new `shared/ui/undo-toast.service.spec.ts`,
+13 `shared/player/detection-overlay-logic.spec.ts` (`detectionModelKey`/`modelHue`/`distinctModelKeys`),
+6 `features/replay/replay-logic.spec.ts` (`capDetectionBuckets`)). `ng test --watch=false` (this is the
one build gate that must go through the Angular CLI's own test builder, not raw `npx vitest run` — see
this file's own Build/test line up top) green throughout. `npx tsc` clean via `ng build`.

**Build**: `ng build` (production) compiles clean — **336.70 kB raw / 94.87 kB transfer initial**, up
+3.45 kB/+0.85 kB from the prior recorded 333.25/94.02 — almost entirely `<vision-undo-toast>` itself
(mounted eagerly at the app root, same as `<vision-toast-host>`); `detection-overlay-logic.ts`'s new
exports only ever reach `player.ts`, which stays lazy-chunk-only as before. **The 300 kB initial-bundle
warning is pre-existing, verified independently of this task**: a clean `git worktree add … HEAD` build
(no uncommitted changes from this or any other concurrent agent) already reported **333.25 kB raw**,
33.25 kB over budget, before this batch's own +3.45 kB — carried since U2's CDK addition (see F-d's own
entry above), not something this task introduced or is in scope to fix. Still comfortably inside the
360 kB error budget (`maximumError`) either way; build exit code 0.

Files touched: `shared/ui/undo-toast.service.ts`/`.spec.ts`, `shared/ui/undo-toast.ts` (new);
`app.ts`/`app.html` (mount); `features/devices/devices.ts`, `features/asset-detail/asset-detail.ts`

### Deviations from the task brief, with reasons

- **The deep link this app actually builds is `/replay?asset=<id>&usage=<id>&t=<offsetMs>`**, not
  the plan's own literal shorthand `/replay?usage=<id>&t=<offsetMs>` (no `asset`). `ReplayPage`
  needs an asset id to fetch device names/telemetry-device grouping (`getAsset(assetId)`); every
  call site that builds this link (`NotificationBell.navigate`, `WallPage.openEvent`) already has
  `event.assetId` in hand at the exact moment it resolves the deep link (no extra lookup), so
  including it costs nothing and avoids a degraded "no device names" rendering that would otherwise
  need its own fallback path. `assetId` is still genuinely *optional* on the flat route (a
  hand-typed URL omitting it degrades gracefully — see `ReplayPage`'s own class doc comment) for
  robustness, but in practice this app never constructs a link without it.
- **Zones management is a modal overlay (`<vision-zones-panel>`), not a third `commandGridColumns`
  grid track.** The plan says "a Zones management panel in Command" without pinning the exact
  layout; a third always-reserved side panel would mean re-touching `command-logic.ts#commandGridColumns`'s
  own tested 2×3 grid arithmetic for a feature used occasionally (draw/rename/delete zones), not
  browsed continuously the way the entity rail/asset panel are — the same "modal, not embedded"
  reasoning `shared/map/fleet-plan-dialog/flight-plan-dialog.ts` already established for flight-plan
  authoring.
- **The zone-draw dialog is create-only** — there is no "Edit boundary" entry on an existing zone
  (only rename/enable-disable/delete, all in the Zones panel's own list). `GeofenceStore.redraw()`
  exists and is fully wired to the API, ready for a future cycle to add that entry; not adding the
  UI for it this batch was a scope call (the plan's own poka-yoke bullets only ask for the draw-new
  flow's own validations, not an edit flow).
- **Command's weather chip always uses the plan's own 10 m/s default limit**, never a specific
  asset's `windLimitMps` override — `AssetAttention` (the fleet-summary row `CommandPage` already
  polls) carries no `attributes` field at all to read one from, and fetching a second per-asset
  lookup just for this one advisory chip was judged disproportionate; Fly's chip (scoped to one
  selected asset, whose `AssetDetails.attributes` this app already has) is the one that honors it.
- **`shared/map/fleet-map/fleet-map.ts`'s own event-marker popup "Details" button was not wired to
  Q1's deep link** — still asset-only, a deliberate scoping call (raw-HTML popups driven by one
  delegated click listener aren't a natural place to host an async `VisionApi` lookup + router
  navigation) documented on that component's own class doc comment and the MODULE.md bullet it
  used to describe as an "unbuildable" gap (now closed elsewhere, just not wired in here).

## I-e Stage 1, wave 3 — "Bring home" UI (docs/DRONE-INFRA-PLAN.md I-e Stage 1's frozen contract)

The RX-only doctrine's one deliberate, guarded exception, staged: a single command,
`MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE → RTL`, reachable from exactly two places (Fly's cockpit HUD, Command's
`AssetPanel`), always behind a mandatory confirm dialog, never optimistic. Wave 1
(`FlightCommandPort`/`MavlinkFlightCommander`, `vision-domain`/`adapter-mavlink`) and wave 2
(`POST /api/assets/{assetId}/return-home`, `FlightCommandController`/`FlightCommandService`,
`vision-api`/`vision-application`) landed in parallel, outside this module's own scope — this wave
was coded against the plan's own frozen wire contract (`202 {result: "ACCEPTED"|"NO_ACK"}` / `404`
/ `409 {message}`) and only cross-checked against the landed backend DTO/controller afterward,
read-only, to confirm the assumption (`ReturnHomeResponse(String result)`,
`POST /api/assets/{id}/return-home`, `@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.ACCEPTED)`) — an exact match, no
rework needed.

**New**: `shared/ui/confirm-dialog.ts`/`.html`/`.css`, `shared/ui/return-home-button.ts`/`.html`/`.css`,
`shared/ui/return-home-button-logic.ts`(+`.spec.ts`). **Reshaped**: `core/api/models.ts`
(`ReturnHomeResult`/`ReturnHomeResponse`), `core/api/vision-api.ts`(+`.spec.ts` — `returnHome(assetId)`),
`core/telemetry/flight-state-logic.ts`(+`.spec.ts` — `canCommandReturnHome`), `core/map/map-logic.ts`
(+`.spec.ts` — `FleetMarker.firmware`), `core/toast.service.ts`(+`.spec.ts` — the new `warning` kind
+ `warn()`), `shared/ui/toast-host.ts` (`.toast.warning` CSS), `features/fly/fly.ts`/`.html`,
`features/command/asset-panel.ts`/`.html`.

- **`core/telemetry/flight-state-logic.ts#canCommandReturnHome(firmware, ageSeconds)`** — the one
  gate, per the plan: `firmware === 'ardupilot'` (INAV masquerades as ArduPilot on the wire — this
  one check is deliberately the *complete* gate, Betaflight/unknown firmware never reports that
  string) **and** telemetry is fresh, reusing `isStale`/`STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` (`core/telemetry/telemetry-logic.ts`)
  directly rather than a second "fresh enough to command" constant. Takes plain `firmware`/`ageSeconds`
  values, not a whole `TelemetrySample` — mirrors `deriveDiagnostics`'s own reasoning: this gate's
  two call sites already have the answer in different shapes (Fly's `TelemetryStore.latest()` sample
  + a `nowMs` read; Command's `FleetMarker`, whose `sampleAgeSeconds` is already precomputed and
  carries no nested `flightState` at all). **Note**: `ageSeconds !== undefined` is checked explicitly
  ahead of `isStale` — `isStale(undefined)` itself returns `false` (its own "unknown, don't assume
  bad" contract), but "no telemetry sample at all" must never read as "fresh enough to command"; the
  two absent-data rules diverge on purpose here (caught by a spec case, not just reasoned about).
- **`core/map/map-logic.ts#FleetMarker` gained `firmware?: string`**, sourced in `buildMarker` from
  the same place `flightMode`/`armed`/`failsafe`/`gpsFixType` already are (the streaming asset's
  latest sample's own `flightState`) — the identical F-d/F-e reuse rationale, needed here because
  `AssetAttention` (the fleet-summary DTO `AssetPanel`'s other inputs come from) carries no firmware
  field at all; this marker-level field is Command's only source.
- **`shared/ui/confirm-dialog.ts`** (`<vision-confirm-dialog>`, new) — the first reusable modal
  confirm in `shared/ui/`: a true `position: fixed` backdrop (`z-index: 150`, mirrors
  `shared/map/fleet-plan-dialog/flight-plan-dialog.ts`'s/`features/command/geofence-zone-dialog.ts`'s
  own convention), not Fly's page-local `.hud-confirm`/`.inline-confirm-card` scrim — needed because
  this dialog has to render correctly from two different host layouts (Fly's full-bleed cockpit,
  Command's docked side panel), neither of which it can lean on. `message`/`confirmLabel`/
  `cancelLabel`/`busy` inputs, `confirmed`/`cancelled` outputs. Deliberately no backdrop-click or
  `Escape` dismissal — every close is an explicit button click, per the plan's own poka-yoke wording
  ("never skippable").
- **`shared/ui/return-home-button.ts`** (`<vision-return-home-button>`, new) — the shared "one
  component, two call sites" button (the same precedent `shared/ui/weather-chip.ts`/
  `shared/player/detections-strip.ts` established), reused verbatim by `FlyPage`/`AssetPanel`.
  Unlike `weather-chip.ts` (host-provided store, no HTTP of its own), this component owns its HTTP
  call and toast directly — `VisionApi`/`ToastService` are both `providedIn: 'root'`, so no
  page-scoped `providers` entry is needed, and there's no shared store a one-shot command like this
  could sensibly live behind. Inputs: `assetId`/`assetDisplayName` (the confirm text —
  `"Command <name> to return home?"`), `canCommand` (the host's own `canCommandReturnHome` verdict —
  gating is the host's job, this component only renders it, hidden entirely when `false`), `compact`
  (mirrors `<vision-player [compact]>`'s naming — both call sites pass `true`, a small `.btn.danger.small`).
  `:host { display: contents }` (mirrors the dialog components' own convention) so the button lands
  as a plain sibling in whatever flex row the host places it in (`fly.html`'s `.hud-header`,
  `asset-panel.html`'s `.panel-actions`), inheriting each row's own button sizing for free. Click →
  `confirmOpen` → `<vision-confirm-dialog>` → on confirm, `busy=true` (disables both dialog buttons
  and the trigger button itself — no double-fire, a plain signal, not a state machine; this is a
  single one-shot request, not a saga with retries the way `player-recovery.ts`'s reconnect logic
  is) → `VisionApi.returnHome(assetId)` → `returnHomeToastFor(result)`'s pure verdict (`shared/ui/return-home-button-logic.ts`,
  new, unit-tested — `ACCEPTED` → `ToastService.ok('Return home commanded')`, `NO_ACK` →
  `ToastService.warn('Command sent — no acknowledgement from aircraft')`) or, on a rejected promise,
  `ToastService.error(describeHttpError(error))` (`core/api-error.ts`'s existing switch already
  surfaces a `409`'s `message` verbatim and a network failure's status-0 case generically — no new
  error decoding needed here). **No optimistic UI, ever** (the plan's own wording): the button's job
  ends the moment the request settles; the aircraft's actual mode change arrives later over ordinary
  telemetry (`flightState.mode` → an RTL-family value), which `flightBanner`/`<vision-failsafe-banner>`
  already turns into "Return to home active" on its own, no wiring needed from this button.
- **`core/toast.service.ts` gained a `warning` kind + `warn(text)`** (no `action`, unlike `ok`/`notify` —
  there's nothing useful to click from a NO_ACK toast) — mirrors E-b's own precedent for adding
  `notification` (own `DISMISS_AFTER_MS` entry, 7s, between `notification`'s 6s and `error`'s 9s;
  own `.toast.warning` CSS in `shared/ui/toast-host.ts`, the app's existing `--warn` amber, distinct
  from `.error`'s red — a NO_ACK command genuinely went out, it isn't a failure).
- **Fly cockpit (`fly.ts`/`.html`)**: `canBringHome` computed (mirrors `preflightItems`'s own
  "re-derives whenever the tracked sample changes, not a continuously-ticking clock" convention) →
  `<vision-return-home-button>` placed in `.hud-header`, right after the drone switcher and before
  the `?` shortcuts button — literally adjacent to (directly below, when it's showing) the failsafe
  banner at the very top edge, and outside `.hud-controls`' Start/Stop/Replay row (a deliberate
  command, not a stream control). No new absolutely-positioned HUD island/offset math needed (the
  header row's own flex layout already has room), unlike `.hud-preflight`/`.hud-diagnostics`'s own
  "approximate, not computed" bottom-row offsets.
- **Command (`asset-panel.ts`/`.html`)**: `canBringHome` computed, fed from `marker()`'s own
  `firmware`/`sampleAgeSeconds` (no second `TelemetryStore` poller — the same reuse this panel's
  Mode/Armed/GPS/diagnostics facts already established) → `<vision-return-home-button>` appended to
  the existing `.row.panel-actions` (Watch live / Details / **Bring home**); `.panel-actions .btn { flex:1 }`
  applies to it for free through the `display: contents` host.
- **Deliberately not extracted as its own reducer**: the button's `busy` guard against
  double-fire/re-entrant clicks is a plain `signal(false)`/try-finally, not a pure state-machine
  file — a single one-shot request has nothing for a reducer to model beyond "in flight or not",
  unlike `player-recovery.ts`'s genuinely multi-transition reconnect saga.

## I-h wave B — SRT + UDP/MPEG-TS ingest in the connect flow (docs/DRONE-INFRA-PLAN.md I-h)

UI half of I-h's low-latency drone video ingest: `srt`/`udp` added to the Register method's
protocol picker, plus small connect-flow polish. Wave A (`adapters/adapter-rtsp/**`,
`FfmpegVideoSource#supports` accepting the two protocol strings) lands concurrently, out of this
task's file scope (`vision-web/**` only) — built against the plan's own frozen contract, not
against that adapter's source.

- **`features/onboarding/protocols.ts`** — `REGISTERABLE_PROTOCOLS` gains two entries:
  - **`srt`** — hint: *"Low-latency drone/FPV video over SRT (4G/5G, long-range links) — the
    drone usually dials in, so set mode=listener under Stream options; leave it as caller to dial
    out to an encoder."* Placeholder **`srt://0.0.0.0:8890`** — a listener URI (this app binds and
    waits), the more common real-world posture per the plan's own reasoning: a field-deployed
    encoder on a dynamic cellular IP dials in to this platform's stable address, not the other way
    around; port 8890 is mediamtx's own well-known default SRT port (this repo already runs
    mediamtx), picked as a recognizable, plausible example rather than an arbitrary number. The
    `mode`/`latency`/`streamid`/`passphrase` knobs from the plan's frozen contract are **not**
    embedded in the placeholder URI as query params — they go through the existing
    `StreamDescriptor.options` key/value editor (see below), the same mechanism `mavlink`'s
    `sysid` option already uses in this exact form; the placeholder therefore stays a bare
    `srt://host:port`, matching the plan's own written form.
  - **`udp`** — hint: *"MPEG-TS over UDP (ground-station encoder, e.g. ffmpeg -f mpegts udp://…) —
    this app listens on the port, it does not dial out."* Placeholder **`udp://0.0.0.0:5600`** —
    5600 is the de facto standard UDP video port in the FPV/drone world (ArduPilot SITL video,
    QGroundControl's default, most gstreamer/ffmpeg drone recipes), the obvious realistic example.
  - Header doc comment's verified-adapter list extended for both — explicitly flagged as sourced
    from the plan's frozen contract, **not** independently re-verified against
    `adapter-rtsp`'s own source (this task's file scope stayed `vision-web/**`), unlike the other
    six entries which were each checked against their adapter's actual `supports()`.
  - **List reordered** (not restructured into `<optgroup>`s): network-stream protocols first
    (`rtsp`, `mjpeg`, `srt`, `udp` — the ones an operator is usually choosing between), then local
    sources (`v4l2`, `file`), then the two special-purpose entries (`sim`, `mavlink`) last. Chose
    plain reordering over visual `<optgroup>` grouping: the register form's `<select>`
    (`onboarding.html`) renders one flat `@for` over `ProtocolOption[]` with no group data on the
    type, and true optgroups would need either a new field (breaking the array's flat shape every
    consumer — `placeholderForProtocol`/`isKnownProtocol`/`protocolSelectionFor` — assumes) or a
    second hand-maintained lookup; each `<option>` already renders `{{ value }} — {{ hint }}`
    inline, judged enough for an 8-item list. `ProtocolOption`'s shape/typing and the three helper
    functions are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **`onboarding.html`** register form, advanced-mode "Stream options" panel (`settings.advancedMode()`
  gate, pre-existing key/value option-row editor, `store.addOptionRow()`/`updateOptionKey`/
  `updateOptionValue` — this *is* the form's one StreamDescriptor-options editor, confirmed before
  writing anything, so no new editor was built) — gained two protocol-conditional inline hint
  paragraphs, `@if (store.protocol() === 'srt')` / `@else if (store.protocol() === 'udp')`,
  spelling out `mode`/`latency` (srt) and the host-filtering/MPEG-TS-assumed behavior + low-latency
  option keys (udp) right next to the option rows an operator would fill in. The `srt` hint's own
  `ProtocolOption.hint` text (visible in the `<select>` even before opening advanced mode) already
  carries the essential listener-vs-caller guidance too — belt-and-suspenders, since advanced mode
  is off by default and the options editor itself is invisible until it's on.
- **Drone-onboarding wizard's `'drone'` Connect method** (docs/DRONE-INFRA-PLAN.md I-g, wave B,
  `drone-config-logic.ts`/`onboarding-store.ts`/`onboarding.html`'s `chooseDroneMethod()` tile) —
  verified, not touched: it builds a hardcoded `protocol: 'mavlink'` device
  (`buildDroneDeviceSpec`) and never reads `REGISTERABLE_PROTOCOLS` at all, so it has no srt/udp
  surface to add — that method is MAVLink-telemetry-only by design (I-g's own scope), unrelated to
  this video-ingest wave. The **register-manually** flow (`chooseMethod('register')`, the only
  place `REGISTERABLE_PROTOCOLS` is rendered — the whole 3/4/5-choice Connect step lives in this
  one wizard now, `features/devices/` no longer renders any of it, see the U-d entry above) picks
  up `srt`/`udp` automatically, protocol-select markup unchanged. The test-before-save probe
  (`POST /api/devices/probe`, Test step) needed no wiring — `buildProbeRequest`
  (`onboarding-logic.ts`) is already protocol-agnostic, forwarding whatever `protocol`/`uri`/
  `options` the form holds.
- **Doc-debt flagged, not fixed here (out of this task's scope)**: I-g wave B itself (commit
  `29230e3`, `drone-config-logic.ts` + the `'drone'` `ConnectMethod`/its wizard sub-step/the
  firmware×link picker) landed with **no MODULE.md entry at all** — this section only covers I-h
  wave B's own changes plus what was read, read-only, to verify against it. A future task should
  add I-g wave B's own entry.

### Tests

`features/onboarding/protocols.spec.ts` only touched (no other spec file changed by this task):
the `REGISTERABLE_PROTOCOLS` array-order assertion updated to the new 8-entry order,
`placeholderForProtocol('srt'/'udp')` assertions added to the existing case, and one new `describe`
block (`srt / udp`, 5 new `it`s) covering `isKnownProtocol`, `protocolSelectionFor`, the srt hint's
`mode=listener`/`caller` content, the udp hint's "listens" content, and a grouping-order assertion
(every network-stream protocol index precedes every local/special one) — **12 → 17 cases in this

## U-AUTH-PLAN wave 4 — login screen, identity chip, auth store, route guard (docs/U-AUTH-PLAN.md)

Real identity's UI half, landed against wave 3's own frozen `MeResponse`/`/api/auth/*` contract, in
parallel with — and without reading — the backend wave. Full permanent reference is the dedicated
`core/auth/**`/`features/auth/login/**`/`identity-chip` section further up this file; this entry is
the narrative: the render-flash decision, dev-parity handling, and the deviations worth recording.

**Avoiding a boot/auth-check render flash.** Two complementary mechanisms, not one:
- **The guard blocks, deliberately.** `authGuard` is `async` and `await`s `AuthStore.ready` (the
  constructor's own `loadMe()` promise) before deciding anything — so the very first navigation of a
  session is always resolved against the network *response*, never the transitional `'loading'`
  default. This trades a small one-time delay (the `GET /api/auth/me` round-trip, typically low
  double-digit ms locally) for a hard guarantee: a protected page is never mounted and then yanked
  to `/login` a beat later, and `/login` is never flashed for a session that turns out to already be
  authed. Every navigation *after* the first pays nothing — `ready` is already a resolved promise.
- **The identity chip renders optimistically-nothing, not a placeholder.** `IdentityChip` shows
  nothing at all while `AuthStore.user()` is `null` (covers both `'loading'` and a genuine anon
  session about to redirect) and simply appears once resolved — there is no skeleton/spinner state
  to swap out, so there's nothing to flash *from*. This is the `shared/ui/weather-chip.ts` precedent
  ("hide entirely rather than show a stale/fake state"), reused rather than inventing a loading UI
  for one header chip.

**Dev-parity (`vision.auth.enabled=false`, the default).** `AuthStore` treats the backend's own
no-op dev-admin response exactly like a real login: `status → 'authed'`, `user` set to that admin,
`authEnabled → false`. Two consequences fall out for free rather than needing special-casing:
`needsLogin` is false unconditionally whenever `authEnabled` is false (checked first, short-circuits
before `status`/`user` are even consulted), so `/login` is genuinely unreachable, not just usually
skipped by the guard; and the identity chip still renders the dev admin's name + role badge (the
plan's own explicit call — "so the surface is consistent"), only suppressing the **Log out** button
itself, since logging out of a session that was never real has nothing to do.

**Identity-chip responsive collapse.** One `<details>` popover, not two templates switched by media
query: the trigger shows avatar + name + role badge inline above 640px; the one breakpoint rule
(matching `app.css`'s own header breakpoint) hides just the name/role *text* in the trigger below
that width, leaving the avatar alone as the tap target. The dropdown menu is never touched by the
breakpoint — it always carries name/role/logout — so collapsing loses no information, only defers it
behind one tap on narrow viewports. Same idiom as `app.css`'s `.tab-more`/`notification-bell.ts`'s
`.bell`, not a new dropdown component.

**`withCredentials` — not needed, confirmed against how this app is actually served.**
vision-web/MODULE.md's own header already states it: this SPA is always same-origin with
vision-api, either the built `dist/` served off vision-app's own classpath (production) or
`ng serve`'s `proxy.conf.json` forwarding `/api` to `:8080` (dev). A same-origin request already
carries the session cookie with no flag needed; `withCredentials` only matters for a genuinely
cross-origin request, which this app has never had reason to make. Not a decision specific to auth —
consistent with the fact no existing `HttpClient` call anywhere in this codebase sets it either.

**A deliberate deviation, documented rather than silently scoped out**: a session that expires
*mid-app* (not at boot) still surfaces as a bare `401` through whichever store's `run()`/poll catch
handles it, and `core/api-error.ts#describeHttpError`'s existing `401` case
("The device rejected these credentials.") is about a *device's* rejected credentials (e.g. a bad
RTSP password), not this app's own expired session — so a mid-session expiry currently reads as a
confusing device-auth toast rather than a redirect to `/login`. The plan's wave-4 scope is the login
screen/chip/store/guard themselves, not a global 401-interceptor/redirect-on-expiry concern (the
guard only ever runs on navigation, not on every HTTP response) — left as a known, scoped gap for a
future task rather than added unasked.

**Tests**: `core/auth/auth-logic.spec.ts` (15 cases — `roleLabel` ×3, `topRoleLabel` ×2, `initialsFor`
×5, `needsLogin`'s full matrix ×5 including the authEnabled=false-always-false sweep across every
status/user combination) + `core/auth/auth-store.spec.ts` (12 cases — boot states incl. the 401→anon
and unreachable-backend→anon paths, dev-parity auto-authed, `login` success/401/other-failure/busy,
`logout` incl. the authEnabled=false→`/fly` routing and the request-fails-but-still-clears-state
path). No dedicated `auth-guard.ts`/component specs — this codebase's own "component specs only as
far as existing precedent goes" rule; the guard is thin wiring over an already fully-covered pure
function, and there is no prior route-guard spec in this app to mirror. **Full suite: 1064/1064
passing** (1037 baseline + 27 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on both `tsconfig.app.json`/
`tsconfig.spec.json`.

**Build**: `ng build --configuration production` compiles clean — **initial total 340.06 kB →
346.04 kB raw / 95.99 kB → 97.73 kB transfer (+5.98 kB raw / +1.74 kB transfer)** — the eager cost of
`AuthStore`+`auth-guard.ts`+`auth-logic.ts` (referenced directly from `app.routes.ts`'s own eager
route config) plus `IdentityChip` (mounted unconditionally in `app.html`'s header, alongside
`NotificationBell`). **`login` lazy chunk: 3.67 kB raw / 1.36 kB transfer** — its own new route,
small as the plan expected ("login/chip should be small, the guard/store are eager"). Pre-existing
budget warnings (300 kB initial, 6 kB `onboarding.css`) both carried from before this task, both
already breached at the prior baseline — this task's own eager addition widens the first by
5.98 kB, doesn't newly trigger it.

**Nothing incomplete against the task's own ask** — the one documented, deliberate scope boundary is
the mid-session-401 gap above, not a missed requirement.

## ASSET-MANAGER-PAGE-PLAN Wave B — asset manager page rework + KPI/utilization dashboards + button-alignment audit (docs/ASSET-MANAGER-PAGE-PLAN.md)

The user's own direction: **the asset detail page is for the manager, not for piloting**. Surveyed
fleet-ops convention (Samsara, Geotab, DJI FlightHub 2, Auterion Suite, Skydio — the plan's own "how
other systems do it" section) is consistent: asset detail is glanceable KPIs/health/history, never a
live control surface; live control is a separate, one-click-away destination. This app already had
that destination (Fly + `/live/:deviceId`) — Wave B's job was removing the duplicate piloting
affordances from the manager page and linking to them, plus adding the KPI/utilization dashboards
those systems lead with. Full permanent reference is the rewritten `features/asset-detail/**` /
`core/fleet/asset-stats-logic.ts` sections further up this file; this entry is the narrative.

**Removed vs. kept.** Removed: the Video card (`<vision-player>`), the Stream info card
(`<vision-stream-info>`), inline Start/Stop stream controls, and every signal/effect that only
existed to drive them (`stopped`/`explicitlyStopped`/`hasBeenLive`/`videoStateLine`/`latencySeconds`/
`transport`/`boxesMode`, plus `DetectionsStore` itself — it had no other reader once the player's
overlay-boxes input was gone). Kept, unchanged: Position (map inset), Telemetry (current readings),
Events (including the live per-stream feed while *someone else* streams the asset — read-only
observation, not piloting), Usage history, Characteristics, Hardware. **This page never mounts a
player or starts/stops a stream again.**

**Cockpit-link band** (replaces the Video/Stream cards' slot): a `live()`/`Offline` chip (reusing the
header's own existing `.chip`/`.dot.live` idiom, no new visual language) plus a primary **Open
cockpit** button (`openCockpit()` — writes `SettingsStore.flyAssetId`, the same field `FlyPage`'s own
picker/switcher write, then navigates to `/fly`; works while offline, since the cockpit owns
start/stop) and a secondary **Watch live** (unchanged `watch()` → `/live/:deviceId`, shown only when
the asset has a video device).

**KPI tile row** — `VisionApi.assetStats(assetId)` (new; `GET /api/assets/{id}/stats`, Wave A's frozen
contract, landed in parallel) feeds `core/fleet/asset-stats-logic.ts#kpiTiles`: five `dataviz` stat
tiles, biggest number first (Total flight time, Flights, Last flown, Avg flight, Battery). Every value
is real or `'—'` — **including Flights** on a failed `/stats` fetch (a bare `0` there would dishonestly
claim "known never flown"); `flightInProgress` marks the flight-time tile with a live pip + "Flying
now". The fetch (`loadStats`) is independent of the page's own `getAsset` load — a `/stats` 404/error
never flips `notFound` or blocks anything else, and on failure it leaves `stats` at its last-known
value (or the initial `undefined`) rather than blanking the row, the same silent-degrade convention
this page's `pollStreamEvents` already used.

**"Recent flights" chart** — one bar per `recentUsages` entry (oldest→newest, `core/fleet/asset-
stats-logic.ts#flightBars`), plain HTML/CSS bars per `dataviz`'s mark spec (16px fixed columns, ≤24px
ceiling; 4px rounded top, square baseline; 2px gaps; one `var(--accent)` hue, no legend needed for a
single series); a live pip on the still-open bar. Honestly labeled "recent flights" (the capped list)
vs. the KPI row's lifetime aggregate. Each bar is focusable with a `title`/`aria-label` (date +
duration); every value is also reachable without hovering in the Usage history table below it (the
chart's table-view twin, per `dataviz`'s "no tooltip-only value" rule) — deliberately not a full custom
tooltip/crosshair layer, given the plan's own "manager glance, not an analytics page" scope. Palette:
no new colors — `var(--accent)` (bars), `var(--live)` (the in-progress pip, via the existing
`.dot.live` class), `var(--text-muted)`/`var(--text-faint)` (labels/axis captions) are all reused
tokens, none invented. Responsive: fixed-width columns + `overflow-x: auto` rather than shrinking bars
to unreadable slivers on narrow viewports.

**Button-alignment audit.** `asset-detail.html`'s own action rows (header, `td.actions`, every
inline-form Save/Cancel pair) were already consistent — primary-first, matched sizing within a row —
so nothing there needed fixing beyond removing the piloting row entirely (the worst offender: a
segmented toggle + a lone default-size button, now gone with the Video card). Fly's `.hud-controls`
and its stop-confirm row were likewise already consistent. **One real inconsistency found and fixed**,
outside asset-detail: `features/command/asset-panel.css`'s `.panel-actions` stretched its two plain
`.btn` children to equal width, a rule that could never reach `<vision-return-home-button>`'s
internally-templated `<button>` (Angular view encapsulation) — see that section's own note above for
the fix (dropped the equal-fill rule; every button, including the encapsulated one, now renders at its
own natural width). No button colors/tokens changed anywhere — alignment/spacing/ordering only.

**Tests**: `core/fleet/asset-stats-logic.spec.ts` (new, 18 cases) — `usageDurationSeconds` (closed,
open-counts-to-now, never negative), `formatFlightTime` (`null`→`'—'`, honest `0`→`'0m'`,
minutes-only, hours+minutes zero-padded, a whole hour), `kpiTiles` (`undefined` stats degrades every
tile including Flights, never-flown asset, a fully-populated response, `flightInProgress`'s live pip +
sub, an honest `0m` total from flights that summed to zero seconds), `flightBars` (empty, one open
usage counted to now, newest-first input reversed to chronological, height scaling against the set's
own max with the floor applied, every-duration-zero flooring every bar). **Full suite: 1082/1082
passing** (1064 baseline + 18 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

**Build**: `ng build --configuration production` compiles clean, same two pre-existing budget warnings
carried from before (300 kB initial, 6 kB `onboarding.css`), neither newly triggered. Bundle delta
(measured via a clean `git worktree` at this task's own starting commit, so removed-Player vs.
added-KPI/chart code isolate cleanly): **`asset-detail` lazy chunk grew, it did not shrink** — 35.21 kB
→ 36.84 kB raw / 8.72 kB → 9.31 kB transfer (+1.63 kB / +0.59 kB). The plan's own text speculated the
player removal *might* reduce this chunk; measured, it didn't, because `<vision-player>`'s heavy
dependency (`hls.js`) was already its own separately-lazy-loaded chunk (unaffected either way) — only
the thin `Player`/`StreamInfoPanel` component *shells* left this chunk, and the new KPI/chart feature
(plus `core/fleet/asset-stats-logic.ts`, single-consumer today, esbuild inlines it here rather than
extracting a shared chunk) outweighs what they cost. Initial bundle total is flat (346.04 kB → 346.12 kB,
noise-level — asset-detail is lazy, uninvolved in the initial chunk). Whole-`dist/` size: +2,219 bytes
(~+0.14%) end to end.

**Nothing incomplete against the task's own ask.** One deliberate scope call worth flagging: the chart
uses native `title`/`aria-label` per bar rather than a custom hover/crosshair tooltip layer
(`dataviz`'s fuller interaction spec) — justified above by the plan's own "keep it small" instruction
and the Usage history table already carrying every value as this chart's table-view twin.

## I-e Stage 2, Wave C — Arm/Disarm/Mode select UI (docs/DRONE-INFRA-PLAN.md I-e Stage 2's frozen contract)

Extends Stage 1's "Bring home" (previous section) with the two next command classes, now
capability-gated per vehicle: **Mode** select, **Arm**, **Disarm** — all in the Fly cockpit, right
beside `<vision-return-home-button>`. Wave A (domain: `FlightCommandPort#setMode`/`arm`/`disarm`,
`FlightCapability`) and wave B (application + `vision-api`: the REST trio + `GET .../flight-
capabilities`) landed in parallel, outside this module's own scope — this wave was coded **only**
against the plan's own frozen wire contract (`GET /api/assets/{id}/flight-capabilities` →
`{commandable, armSupported, modeSelectSupported, selectableModes}`; `POST .../mode {mode}` /
`.../arm {force?}` / `.../disarm {force?}` → `202 {result}`; `404`/`409 {message}`/`400`/`403`), no
backend files read or waited on, mirroring Stage 1's own wave-3 precedent exactly.

**New**: `core/api/models.ts` (`FlightCommandResult`/`FlightCommandResponse`/`FlightCapability`),
`core/api/vision-api.ts`(+`.spec.ts` — `flightCapabilities(assetId)`/`setMode(assetId, mode)`/
`arm(assetId, force?)`/`disarm(assetId, force?)`), `features/fly/flight-command-panel-logic.ts`
(+`.spec.ts`), `features/fly/flight-command-panel.ts`/`.html`/`.css`,
`features/fly/arm-confirm-dialog.ts`/`.html`/`.css`. **Reshaped**: `features/fly/fly.ts`/`.html`/`.css`.

- **`features/fly/flight-command-panel-logic.ts`** (new, pure, unit-tested) — `canShowCommandPanel(capabilities,
  firmware, ageSeconds)` = `capabilities !== undefined && capabilities.commandable &&`
  `flight-state-logic.ts#canCommandReturnHome(firmware, ageSeconds)` — the identical firmware+
  freshness bar "Bring home" already clears, extended with the new capability read; `capabilities`
  `undefined` (not yet loaded, or the fetch failed) alone hides the whole panel, no separate loading
  state. `modeConfirmMessage`/`armWarningMessage`/`armFinalConfirmLabel`/`disarmConfirmMessage` are
  the confirm-copy builders (see the components below for how each is used); `commandOutcomeToast(result,
  action)` mirrors `shared/ui/return-home-button-logic.ts#returnHomeToastFor`'s exact shape, one
  `ACCEPTED`/`NO_ACK` pair of sentences per action (`'Mode set'`/`'Armed'`/`'Disarmed'` vs. each
  action's own "… sent — no acknowledgement from aircraft"). **Lives beside its one component under
  `features/fly/`, not `core/telemetry/` or `shared/ui/`** — this wave's UI is Fly-only per the plan's
  own frozen scope (Command's `AssetPanel` is not part of it), so this follows the codebase's own
  "second consumer moves it to a shared home" precedent rather than promoting it early.
- **`features/fly/flight-command-panel.ts`** (`<vision-flight-command-panel>`, new) — same shape as
  `shared/ui/return-home-button.ts`: owns its own HTTP calls + toasts directly (`VisionApi`/
  `ToastService` both `providedIn: 'root'`), gating is the host's job (`canCommand` input, hidden
  entirely when `false`), no optimistic UI (a confirm only ever sends the command and reports
  `ACCEPTED`/`NO_ACK`/an error — the aircraft's actual armed state/mode arrives later over ordinary
  telemetry, which the OSD chips/`flightBanner` already render on their own). Renders a single
  frosted-pill `.command-cluster` (mirrors `fly.css#.switcher-control`'s own chrome) rather than
  three loose buttons: a Mode `<select>` + "Set" (only when `capabilities.modeSelectSupported` and
  `selectableModes` is non-empty; per-`<option>` `[selected]`, not a bound `[value]` on the `<select>`
  itself — the same QF-1 `<select>`/`@for`-ordering-race avoidance `fly.html`'s own drone switcher
  established) and Arm/Disarm buttons (only when `capabilities.armSupported`) — each opens its own
  confirm, `<vision-confirm-dialog>` for Mode/Disarm, the new `<vision-arm-confirm-dialog>` for Arm.
  **One combined `anyBusy` guard disables every trigger button**, not just each one's own — these
  three commands all target the same physical vehicle, so this rules out firing two at once (e.g.
  Arm while a mode-change is still in flight) entirely, a deliberately stricter rule than Stage 1's
  single-button `busy` (which only ever had one control to guard).
- **`features/fly/arm-confirm-dialog.ts`** (`<vision-arm-confirm-dialog>`, new) — the plan's own
  safety framing ("arming spins propellers — the highest-danger action in the app… materially
  higher-friction than RTL's") realized as **a separate component from `shared/ui/confirm-dialog.ts`**,
  not a variant/flag on it, two ways: (1) **a second explicit stage**, not one click — opens on
  `'warn'` (the warning text + a plain neutral "Continue" button, not yet the dangerous action) and
  only advances to `'final'` (the real `armFinalConfirmLabel` button) on that click, so a reflexive
  double-click on open lands on "Continue", never "Arm"; (2) **reserves the app's full, undiluted
  `--live` red** — the exact hue `features/fly/failsafe-banner.ts`'s genuine-failsafe strip uses,
  and nothing else in this app's button chrome does — for the dialog's border/header and the one
  filled (not outline) danger button in the whole app, `.btn.arm-final`. Every other danger-adjacent
  control in this cluster (`.btn.danger` — Arm/Disarm's own trigger buttons, Mode/Disarm's plain
  `<vision-confirm-dialog>`) stays the calmer transparent `--danger` outline, per the plan's own
  "reserve the full `--live` red for the arm modal" instruction — `--live` is now this app's other
  full-strength surface, by design, not a repaint of `--danger`.
- **Disarm's crash-warning derivation** (`disarmConfirmMessage`) — the plan asks for an airborne
  check "if cleanly derivable from what flight-state-logic exposes." It isn't: `FlightState` carries
  no `inAir`/`landed` flag anywhere in the wire contract, and `TelemetrySample.altitudeMeters` alone
  is not a safe stand-in (absolute-vs-relative and home-point-dependent by firmware — a grounded
  vehicle can still report a nonzero reading), so inventing a threshold here would be exactly the
  fabricated-confidence read `flight-state-logic.ts`'s own poka-yoke rule refuses elsewhere. Per the
  plan's own documented fallback, this warns on `flightState.armed === true` alone, worded honestly
  ("if it's currently flying…") rather than asserting airborne state it doesn't actually have.
- **`fly.ts`**: `capabilities` signal (`FlightCapability | undefined`) + `canShowCommands` computed
  (mirrors `canBringHome`'s own "re-derive whenever the tracked sample changes" convention) feed the
  new panel. A new constructor effect fetches capabilities once per asset selection **and** again
  the first time this vehicle's own firmware becomes known (an unheard vehicle reports
  `commandable=false` until its first heartbeat — refetching once firmware resolves is what flips a
  just-connected vehicle's panel from hidden to shown without a manual refresh) — guarded on a
  composite `${assetId} ${firmware}` key via the existing `trackingIdChanged` (mirrors
  `core/live/live-fallback-logic.ts#trackSessionKey`'s own composite-key idiom), the same
  `Object.is`-poll-tick-churn guard this file's telemetry/detections effects already use
  (docs/REALTIME-PLAN.md Phase R-a item 2) — without it, every ~5s `refreshPoll` tick would re-fetch
  capabilities with an unchanged firmware value forever. `loadCapabilities` silent-degrades to
  `undefined` on any failure (404/403/network) — no toast, mirrors `TelemetryStore`/`DetectionsStore`'s
  own "best-effort background read" convention, not `loadAsset`'s user-facing error (the plan's own
  "degrade to hidden if the capabilities call fails" instruction).
- **`fly.html`**: `<vision-flight-command-panel>` placed immediately after `<vision-return-home-button>`
  in `.hud-header`, fed `capabilities()`/`canShowCommands()`/`telemetry.latest()?.flightState?.armed`.
  **`fly.css#.hud-header` gained `flex-wrap: wrap`** — this row now carries a fourth pill-shaped
  control group alongside the switcher/"Bring home"/"?", past what the row's original `nowrap` layout
  was tuned for; wrapping (not clipping off-screen) is the safe default now.
- **Command's `AssetPanel` is untouched** — the plan's own frozen "UI — Wave C" scope names only the
  Fly cockpit for this wave; `shared/ui/return-home-button.ts` (Stage 1) still reuses across both,
  unaffected.
- **403/409 surfacing needed no new code**: `core/api-error.ts#describeHttpError`'s existing switch
  already renders a `403` as "You do not have access to that." and a `409`'s `message` verbatim (the
  identical cases Stage 1's `returnHome` already exercises) — every one of the three new confirm
  handlers' `catch` blocks calls it unchanged, same as `ReturnHomeButton`'s own.
- **Deliberately not extracted as reducers**: each of the three busy guards (`modeBusy`/`armBusy`/
  `disarmBusy`) plus `ArmConfirmDialog`'s own two-stage `stage` signal are plain signals, not a state
  machine file — mirrors Stage 1's own "a single one-shot request has nothing for a reducer to model"
  reasoning, extended to a two-stage-but-still-linear flow.

### Tests

**1099/1099 → 1119/1119** (+20, all pure-logic; no new component-level specs for
`FlightCommandPanel`/`ArmConfirmDialog`, matching this codebase's own standing precedent for dumb
HUD/panel pieces — `ReturnHomeButton`/`ConfirmDialog`/`FailsafeBanner` all have none either):

`tsconfig.app.json`/`tsconfig.spec.json`.

`ng build --configuration production`: **350.01 kB raw / 99.43 kB transfer initial** — up only
